  - [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
  - [Option A: One-Click Launch (Docker Compose)](#option-a-one-click-launch-docker-compose)
  - [Option B: Manual Development Environment](#option-b-manual-development-environment)
- [REST API Reference & Status Codes](#-rest-api-reference--status-codes)
- [Database Schema & Data Dictionary](#-database-schema--data-dictionary)
- [Privacy, Ethics & DPDP Compliance](#-privacy-ethics--dpdp-compliance)
- [Quality Benchmarks & Test Acceptance Plan](#-quality-benchmarks--test-acceptance-plan)
- [Literature References](#-literature-references)
- [License & Contributors](#-license--contributors)

---

## 💡 Key Motivations & Problem Statement

Conventional college administration workflows suffer from structural vulnerabilities:

| Challenge in Legacy Systems | Real-World Impact | IntelliCampus Solution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Attendance Fraud & Proxies** | Roll-calls waste 10–15 mins/lecture; static QR codes and proxy buddies undermine academic integrity. | **Dual-Factor Attendance**: One-shot classroom photo analyzed by InsightFace + anti-spoofing; student confirms within 2 mins via device binding & classroom geofence. Dynamic rotating QR fallback (15s HMAC). |
| **Silent Mark Manipulations** | Internal marks altered in spreadsheets or relational databases with zero immutable history. | **Cryptographic Hash Chain**: Every grade change creates an insert-only SHA-256 block linking to the previous entry, with mandatory audit reason. |
| **Scattered Communications** | Important circulars posted randomly across physical boards, WhatsApp groups, and unstructured portals. | **Targeted Notices & Tracking**: Segmented notifications by department, year, and division with read-receipt audit and automated deadline alerts. |
| **Office Queues for Routine Queries** | Administrative staff repeatedly field identical routine queries about syllabus, exam fees, and deadlines. | **Document-Grounded RAG Chatbot**: Spring AI RAG system that answers strictly from verified PDFs with exact citations (English, Hindi, Marathi). |
| **Reactive Dropout Interventions** | Struggling students are noticed only when semester failure lists or detention notices appear. | **Weekly Early Warning System (EWS)**: Machine learning model (Random Forest / Logistic Regression) evaluates 6 indicators weekly, alerting mentors to top risk drivers. |
| **Certificate / Receipt Forgery** | Hard-copy fee receipts and paper bonafides are vulnerable to tampering and time-consuming manual validation. | **Public Verification**: PDF documents issued with cryptographically signed QR codes and hashes; instantly verifiable online without authentication. |
| **Unlinked Paper Leave Requests** | Physical leave slips lost in transit, resulting in unfair student attendance shortages. | **Integrated Multi-Step Leave Workflow**: Multi-tier approvals (Mentor → HOD) automatically recompute session denominators in attendance calculations. |

---

## 🏛️ System Architecture & Data Flow

IntelliCampus uses a **modular monolith** backend paired with a dedicated **Python AI service**, prioritizing high maintainability, low deployment complexity, and strict horizontal separation of concerns.

```
                           +------------------------------------------+
                           |           React 18 Web Client            |
                           |  (Admin / HOD / Faculty / Mentor / Stud) |
                           +--------------------+---------------------+
                                                |
                                    HTTPS REST / WSS STOMP
                                                |
                                                v
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                    Spring Boot 3 Backend API                                       |
|                                                                                                    |
|  +--------------+  +--------------+  +---------------+  +--------------+  +---------------------+  |
|  |  auth & rbac |  | admin-mgmt   |  |  attendance   |  |  marks-audit |  | notices & notify    |  |
|  +--------------+  +--------------+  +---------------+  +--------------+  +---------------------+  |
|  +--------------+  +--------------+  +---------------+  +--------------+  +---------------------+  |
|  | leave-mgmt   |  | docs-verify  |  | chatbot (RAG) |  | risk-engine  |  | audit hash-chain    |  |
|  +--------------+  +--------------+  +---------------+  +--------------+  +---------------------+  |
+-------------------+-------------------------+---------------------------------+--------------------+
                    |                         |                                 |
           JDBC over TLS               Redis Protocol                   Internal REST API
                    |                         |                                 |
                    v                         v                                 v
        +-----------------------+   +-------------------+          +-------------------------+
        |     MySQL 8.0 DB      |   |      Redis 7      |          | Python 3.11 AI Service  |
        |  - Relational Schema  |   | - Dynamic QR HMAC |          | - InsightFace (512-dim) |
        |  - JSON Biometrics    |   | - Rate Limiters   |          | - Anti-Spoofing Scorer  |
        |  - JSON Document RAG  |   | - Session Caching |          | - Scikit-Learn EWS      |
        |  - Immutable Audit    |   +-------------------+          +-------------------------+
        +-----------------------+
```

---

## 👥 Role-Based Access & Actor Matrix

The system specifies **six distinct user classes** with strict role enforcement enforced at both the API filter level and method security annotations (`@PreAuthorize`):

```
                                  [ College Platform ]
                                           |
         +-----------------+---------------+----------------+----------------+
         |                 |               |                |                |
     [ Admin ]          [ HOD ]        [ Faculty ]      [ Mentor ]      [ Student ]      [ Public Verifier ]
         |                 |               |                |                |                   |
   User Management,   Department      Classroom        Mentee Groups,   Self Dashboard,    Zero Login,
   Academic Setup,    Reports,        Attendance,      Risk Alerts &    2-Min Attendance   QR & Code
   Circulars,         Leave Final,    Marks Entry &    Actions,         Confirm, Disputing, Verifier
   Document Issue     Mark Correction Corrections      Leave 1st Step   Chatbot, Leave
```

| Role | Administrative Scope | Primary Functional Permissions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Admin** | Campus-Wide System & Setup | User account provisioning & bulk CSV import; Academic layout (Departments, Divisions, Subjects, Classrooms with GPS coords); Circular publishing; Document issuance & revocation; Knowledge base indexing. |
| **HOD** | Department Head | Review & approve mark correction requests; Final authorization on leave requests (>3 days); Inspect departmental attendance/defaulter/audit analytics. |
| **Faculty** | Subject Teacher | Open attendance sessions; Live camera class snapshot capture; Resolve student attendance disputes; Enter internal marks; Publish class-specific notices. |
| **Mentor** | Assigned Student Cohort | Monitor assigned mentee progress; Receive automated EWS High-Risk alerts with top feature contributions; Log intervention notes; First-level leave approval. |
| **Student** | Personal Cohort Member | 2-minute attendance confirmation; Rotating QR scanning fallback; View subject-wise attendance & raise disputes; View marks history; Submit leave; Ask RAG chatbot; Download verified receipts. |
| **Public Verifier** | Unauthenticated External | Zero login required. Verify validity, issuance date, and masked student identity of certificates and receipts via code or QR scanner. |

---

## 🔬 Core Functional Innovations

### 1. Dual-Factor AI Attendance Validation Pipeline

To completely eliminate proxy attendance while finishing class marking in **under 2 minutes**, IntelliCampus applies a strict multi-layer sequential validation pipeline:

```
[Faculty Starts Session] ---> [Challenge Code Displayed] ---> [Live In-App Camera Only]
                                                                      |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |
  +---> [1. Time Window Check]       : Must be within 10 minutes of session launch.
  +---> [2. Geofence Radius Check]   : Haversine distance between phone & room GPS <= radius (default 50m).
  +---> [3. Anti-Replay SHA-256]     : File hash verified against past sessions (blocks re-upload).
  +---> [4. Perceptual Hash (pHash)] : 64-bit DCT pHash Hamming distance > 8 (blocks cropped/resized photos).
  +---> [5. InsightFace Extraction]  : Multi-face 512-dim normalized embedding extraction.
  +---> [6. Spoof Detection]        : Anti-spoofing CNN scores face liveness; < 0.60 sent to Review.
  +---> [7. Cosine Search in Vector] : Matches division embeddings via cosine similarity (similarity >= 0.50, margin >= 0.05).
  +---> [8. WebSocket Push to Mentees]: Matched students receive push notification on `/user/queue/attendance`.
  +---> [9. 2-Minute Confirmation]   : Student confirms from approved device fingerprint inside classroom geofence.
  +---> [10. Dynamic QR Fallback]    : Unmatched students scan 15-second rotating HMAC-SHA256 teacher QR code.
  +---> [11. Finalize & Flags]       : Teacher reviews 4 segmented lists and locks session into immutable audit log.
```

#### Attendance Status Lifecycle

```
             +------------+
             |  PENDING   |
             +-----+------+
                   |
         +---------+---------+
         |                   |
         v                   v
   +-----------+       +------------+
   |  MATCHED  |       | UNMATCHED  |
   +-----+-----+       +-----+------+
         |                   |
    +----+----+         +----+----+
    |         |         |         |
    v         v         v         v
+-------+ +---------+ +--------+ +--------+
|PRESENT| |NOT CONF | | REVIEW | | ABSENT |
+-------+ +---------+ +--------+ +--------+
```

- **PRESENT**: Face recognized above threshold **AND** confirmed on registered device inside classroom geofence within 120 seconds.
- **PRESENT_QR**: Validated via high-frequency rotating dynamic QR code inside classroom geofence.
- **REVIEW**: Low facial match confidence, spoof score `< 0.60`, multiple faces mapped to single ID, or dual confirmations from single device fingerprint.
- **ABSENT**: Unrecognized, unconfirmed, or manually marked absent.

---

### 2. Hash-Chained Tamper-Evident Marks & Audit Trail

All administrative modifications—especially internal exam marks, attendance overrides, and credential revocations—are written to an append-only, tamper-evident hash chain inspired by blockchain blocks:

$$\text{entry\_hash} = \text{SHA-256}(\text{prev\_hash} + \text{actor\_id} + \text{action} + \text{entity\_type} + \text{entity\_id} + \text{old\_val} + \text{new\_val} + \text{reason} + \text{created\_at})$$

- **Genesis Block**: Seeded with a deterministic constant hash.
- **Integrity Validation Engine**: Administrators can execute `/api/audit/verify` at any time. The engine recalculates sequential block digests across 10,000+ entries in under 30 seconds, immediately highlighting the exact broken row index if database records were modified directly via SQL.
- **Mandatory Justification**: Any manual status or mark modification requires a descriptive reason string of at least 10 characters.

---

### 3. Multilingual Document-Grounded RAG Chatbot

The IntelliCampus knowledge engine replaces noisy, uncurated chat channels with a hallucination-free, retrieval-augmented system:
- **PDF Ingestion & Chunking**: Institutional PDFs (circulars, syllabi, fee structures, ordinances) are parsed into 500-token passages with a 50-token sliding overlap.
- **Vector Search**: Passages are vectorized and indexed for cosine similarity retrieval.
- **Grounded Generation**: Questions are embedded, retrieving the top 5 cosine-similar chunks. LLM queries run with `temperature = 0.0` with explicit system prompt restrictions:
  > *"You are the IntelliCampus official assistant. Answer ONLY using the supplied context excerpts. Always cite Document Title and Page Number. If the context does not contain the answer, politely refuse and instruct the student to contact the academic registrar."*
- **Multilingual Support**: Supports queries and responses in **English, Hindi, and Marathi**.

---

### 4. Early Warning System (EWS) Machine Learning

A scheduled background job analyzes student academic telemetry weekly to flag early indicators of student attrition:
- **Feature Vector**:
  1. Cumulative attendance percentage
  2. 4-week delta in attendance rate ($\Delta \text{Attn}$)
  3. Internal assessment average percentage
  4. Test score trend relative to previous term ($\Delta \text{Marks}$)
  5. Active academic backlog count
  6. Cumulative approved/unapproved leave days in the prior 30 days
- **Algorithms**: **Random Forest Classifier** alongside an explainable **Logistic Regression Baseline** trained on student academic benchmarks.
- **Risk Tiers**:
  - **Low Risk** ($< 0.33$)
  - **Medium Risk** ($0.33 - 0.66$)
  - **High Risk** ($> 0.66$): Automatically dispatches an alert to the designated mentor displaying the top 3 contributing risk factors. Mentors must document intervention action notes.

---

### 5. Publicly Verifiable Documents (Anti-Forgery)

- **Tamper-Evident Issuance**: Generates official fee receipts, bonafide certificates, and grade transcripts as signed PDFs containing a unique document UUID, SHA-256 digest, and high-density QR code.
- **Zero-Login Verification Page**: Third parties (employers, banks, universities) scan the QR or submit the code at `/verify`.
- **Privacy Masking**: The public verification endpoint confirms document legitimacy (`VALID`, `REVOKED`, or `NOT_FOUND`) while displaying masked student information (e.g., `J*** D**`, Roll `CS***42`) to safeguard student privacy.

---

### 6. Multi-Tier Leave Management System

- **Digital Submissions**: Students submit leave requests specifying dates, category, justification, and optional documentary evidence (up to 5 MB).
- **Two-Stage Approval Chain**:
  - Leaves $\le 3$ days: Handled directly by student's designated Faculty Mentor.
  - Leaves $> 3$ days: Evaluated by Faculty Mentor, then forwarded to Head of Department (HOD) for final approval.
- **Automated Attendance Normalization**: Approved leave dates are automatically credited into attendance calculations, ensuring students are not unfairly designated as attendance defaulters.

---

### 7. Targeted Circulars & Push Notifications

- **Granular Audience Targeting**: Notices can be dispatched to specific scopes: College-wide, Department, Academic Year, or specific Division.
- **Read Receipt Auditing**: Faculty and administration can monitor real-time read statistics (percentage and student list).
- **Automated Deadline Watchdog**: Scheduled task dispatches push alerts 24 hours prior to notice submission deadlines to all students who haven't acknowledged the notice.

---

## 🛠️ Technology Stack Matrix

```
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                    TECHNOLOGY STACK                                    |
+---------------------+-------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Layer               | Technology                    | Purpose                          |
+---------------------+-------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Backend Runtime     | Java 21 LTS (OpenJDK)         | Core business logic monolith     |
| Backend Framework   | Spring Boot 3.2.x             | REST APIs, Dependency Injection  |
| Security & Auth     | Spring Security 6, JWT, BCrypt| RBAC, Access/Refresh tokens      |
| Real-time Messaging | Spring WebSocket + STOMP      | Push attendance & alerts         |
| AI Microservice     | Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn | Face recognition & ML inference  |
| Biometrics / Vision | InsightFace (ArcFace), OpenCV | 512-dim embedding & anti-spoof   |
| Machine Learning    | Scikit-Learn, NumPy, Pandas   | Early Warning Risk Classifier    |
| Primary Database    | MySQL 8.0 / 8.4 LTS           | Relational data & JSON storage   |
| In-Memory Cache     | Redis 7 Alpine                | OTPs, dynamic QR, rate limits    |
| AI Orchestration    | Spring AI (RAG Engine)        | Vector search & LLM prompt chain |
| Frontend Library    | React 18, Vite / CRA          | Single-page web application      |
| Styling & UI        | Tailwind CSS / Lucide Icons   | Responsive mobile-first UI       |
| Hardware Scanner    | html5-qrcode, qrcode.react    | In-app QR generation & camera    |
| Containerization    | Docker, Docker Compose        | Multi-container orchestration    |
| API Documentation   | OpenAPI 3.0 / Springdoc       | Interactive Swagger UI reference |
+---------------------+-------------------------------+----------------------------------+
```

---

## 🚀 Getting Started & Local Setup

### Prerequisites

Ensure the following tools are installed on your workstation:
- **Docker Engine** (v24.0+) & **Docker Compose** (v2.20+)
- **Java Development Kit (JDK 21 LTS)** *(for local backend dev)*
- **Node.js (v20 LTS)** & **npm** *(for local frontend dev)*
- **Python 3.11** *(for local AI service dev)*
- **MySQL 8.0+** *(if running outside Docker)*

---

### Option A: One-Click Launch (Docker Compose)

The fastest method to launch the entire IntelliCampus ecosystem:

1. **Clone the repository**:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/vaishnavibodakhe/IntelliCampus.git
   cd IntelliCampus
   ```

2. **Configure environment variables**:
   Create a `.env` file in the project root:
   ```env
   # MySQL Database
   DB_HOST=db
   DB_PORT=3306

   # Redis Cache
   REDIS_HOST=redis
   REDIS_PORT=6379

   # JWT Security
   JWT_SECRET=4c8a91f2b6e3d7a8c1f4e5a9b2d8c3e7f1a5b9c2d8e4f1a7b3c9d5e2f8a4b6c1
   JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRATION_MS=900000        # 15 minutes
   JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRATION_MS=604800000    # 7 days

   # AI Service Endpoints
   AI_SERVICE_URL=http://ai-service:8000

   # LLM Provider (Hosted or Local Ollama)
   SPRING_AI_OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_or_placeholder
   SPRING_AI_OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com
   ```

3. **Build and spin up all containers**:
   ```bash
   docker-compose up --build -d
   ```

4. **Verify running services**:
   ```bash
   docker-compose ps
   ```

| Container | Service | Host Port | Internal Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `intellicampus-web` | Frontend Web UI | `http://localhost:3000` | Nginx reverse proxy serving React app |
| `intellicampus-api` | Backend API Monolith | `http://localhost:8080` | Spring Boot 3 Core Server |

### Option B: Manual Development Environment

#### 4. React Frontend Web Application

---

## 🌐 REST API Reference & Status Codes

All API endpoints follow RESTful design rooted at `/api`. Dates follow ISO-8601 UTC.

| HTTP Method | Route | Role | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | Public | Authenticates user; returns JWT token & user role. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/refresh` | Public | Exchanges HTTP-only cookie refresh token for new access token. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/users/import` | Admin | Bulk user creation via CSV file with line-level validation. |
| `POST` | `/api/students/{id}/face` | Student/Admin | Enrolls face embeddings (3 live photos) with explicit consent. |
| `POST` | `/api/sessions/start` | Faculty | Initializes class attendance session and challenge code. |
| `POST` | `/api/sessions/{id}/photo` | Faculty | Ingests classroom photo, validates geofence, and triggers AI. |
| `POST` | `/api/attendance/{sessionId}/confirm` | Student | 2-minute geofenced student attendance confirmation. |
| `POST` | `/api/attendance/{sessionId}/qr` | Student | Fallback dynamic QR attendance scan inside room. |
| `POST` | `/api/attendance/{sessionId}/override` | Faculty | Manual override with mandatory justification ($\ge 10$ chars). |
| `POST` | `/api/sessions/{id}/finalise` | Faculty | Locks session, generates anomaly flags, commits audit log. |
| `POST` | `/api/marks` | Faculty | Enters internal marks in draft state. |
| `POST` | `/api/marks/{id}/correction` | Faculty | Submits correction request for published locked marks. |
| `PUT` | `/api/marks/corrections/{id}/decision` | HOD | Authorizes or rejects faculty mark correction request. |
| `GET` | `/api/audit/verify` | Admin | Recalculates cryptographic SHA-256 chain across audit blocks. |
| `POST` | `/api/notices` | Staff | Dispatches targeted notice with departmental segmentation. |
| `POST` | `/api/chat/ask` | Logged In | RAG chatbot query returning document-grounded citation. |
| `GET` | `/api/risk/mentees` | Mentor | Retrieves mentee risk ratings, trends, and alert indicators. |
| `POST` | `/api/documents/issue` | Admin | Issues verifiable PDF credential with embedded QR digest. |
| `GET` | `/api/verify/{code}` | Public | Unauthenticated verification of document authenticity status. |
| `POST` | `/api/leave` | Student | Submits digital leave request with date range and attachment. |
| `PUT` | `/api/leave/{id}/decision` | Mentor/HOD | Evaluates leave approval at appropriate tier. |

### Standardized System Error Codes

| Error Code | HTTP Status | Root Cause |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 Unauthorized | Incorrect user code or password. |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | 423 Locked | Exceeded 5 failed login attempts (locked 15 mins). |
| `FORBIDDEN_ROLE` | 403 Forbidden | User lacks necessary RBAC permissions. |
| `WINDOW_CLOSED` | 410 Gone | Class photo or confirmation window expired. |
| `OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE` | 422 Unprocessable | Device GPS coordinates exceed room radius boundary. |
| `DUPLICATE_PHOTO` | 422 Unprocessable | Exact image SHA-256 match identified from previous sessions. |
| `NEAR_DUPLICATE_PHOTO` | 422 Unprocessable | Image DCT pHash Hamming distance $\le 8$ (resized/cropped). |
| `DEVICE_NOT_APPROVED` | 403 Forbidden | Student confirmation attempted from unverified device. |
| `AI_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 Bad Gateway | Python AI microservice failed to respond. |
| `REASON_REQUIRED` | 400 Bad Request | Justification text is shorter than 10 required characters. |
| `MARKS_PUBLISHED` | 409 Conflict | Direct edits rejected; requires formal HOD correction. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 Not Found | Requested entity, session, or document code not found. |

---

## 🔒 Privacy, Ethics & DPDP Compliance

IntelliCampus is intentionally architected to strictly adhere to **India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023**:

1. **Informed Digital Consent**: Biometric enrollment cannot be triggered without an affirmative, cryptographically recorded student consent action (`consent_at`, `consent_version`).
2. **Zero Raw Image Retention**: Raw facial photographs captured during attendance are processed purely in ephemeral memory and discarded immediately upon 512-dimension vector extraction. No raw facial images are stored on disk or database.
3. **Encryption at Rest**: Face vectors stored in the database are encrypted at rest using **AES-GCM-256** with encryption keys maintained in environment secret vaults outside the database.
4. **Purpose Limitation & Right to Erasure**: Biometric embeddings are strictly utilized for attendance validation and never repurposed. Students possess the irrevocable right to withdraw consent; an administrative action immediately purges all biometric records.
5. **Privacy by Default for Public Verification**: Public document validation outputs only masked credentials, preventing identity theft while proving authenticity.
6. **No Continuous GPS Surveillance**: Geolocation coordinates are requested exclusively at the instantaneous moment of attendance submission to establish classroom presence and are never continuously tracked.

---

## 🧪 Quality Benchmarks & Test Acceptance Plan

The platform is evaluated against rigorous acceptance thresholds:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MATRIX                               |
+--------+---------------------+-------------------------------+--------------------------+
| Code   | Quality Attribute   | Engineering Benchmark         | Verification Method      |
+--------+---------------------+-------------------------------+--------------------------+
| NFR-01 | Vision Speed        | $\le 30$ seconds for 60 faces | Timed stress benchmark   |
| NFR-02 | API Response Time   | 95% of queries $\le 2.0$s     | JMeter (200 concurrent)  |
| NFR-03 | Channel Encryption  | 100% HTTPS TLS 1.3 / WSS      | Automated security audit |
| NFR-04 | Access Control      | 100% server-side role check   | Integration test matrix  |
| NFR-07 | Log Immutability    | 100% detect altered db row    | Cryptographic validator  |
| NFR-08 | Match Safety        | Zero wrong-match accepted     | Volunteer test dataset   |
| NFR-09 | Teacher Workflow    | Completed in $\le 5$ clicks   | Real-world usability trial|
| NFR-11 | System Portability  | 1-step `docker-compose up`    | Clean VM verification    |
+--------+---------------------+-------------------------------+--------------------------+
```

---

## 📚 Literature References

1. **Early Warning Systems**: *Machine Learning in Higher Education: Predicting and Mitigating Student Attrition*, IEEE, 2024. *(Random Forest and Decision Trees for early dropout detection).*
2. **Document-Grounded Chatbots**: *Development and Evaluation of a University Chatbot: A RAG-Based Approach*, Ulster University, 2025. *(Retrieval-augmented grounding reduces hallucination).*
3. **Fraud-Resistant Biometrics**: *AttendEase: Fraud-Resistant Attendance Tracking*, IJACSA. *(Multi-factor verification combining dynamic QR, geofencing, and biometrics).*
4. **Verifiable Academic Records**: *Academic Certificate Validation Using Blockchain Technology*, IEEE, 2022. *(Hash-based tamper-evident credential verification).*

# Deep Learning

This repository is a step-by-step deep learning study project built completely from scratch. Each chapter explores fundamental deep learning concepts by implementing the underlying mathematics and algorithms using **Python and NumPy** before moving to high-level frameworks.

---

## Chapter 1 — Artificial Neural Networks

**Status: Completed**

The goal of Chapter 1 was to master the basic mechanics of an artificial neural network by constructing the entire forward and backward propagation pipeline from scratch.

### What We Built
- Computational neurons with weights and bias
- ReLU, Leaky ReLU, and Sigmoid activation functions with derivatives
- Dense layers and vectorized forward propagation ($Z = XW + b$)
- Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss
- Analytical backpropagation using the chain rule
- Mini-batch training with shuffled indices
- Custom optimizers: SGD, Momentum, and Adam (with bias correction)
- Numerical vs. analytical gradient checking
- XOR gate non-linear learning experiment (`2-4-1` architecture)
- Adam vs. SGD optimizer convergence comparison

### Results
- The network successfully learned the non-linear XOR function.
- Diagnosed and resolved the dying ReLU problem by transitioning to Leaky ReLU.
- Gradient checking verified backpropagation implementation with minimal numerical difference.

---

## Chapter 2 — Data, Regression & Regularization

**Status: Completed**

Chapter 2 focuses on data preparation, feature engineering, non-linear regression, and a comprehensive arsenal of regularization techniques to prevent overfitting, culminating in a real-world motor performance prediction system.

### What We Built
- **Data Splitting & Leakage Prevention:** `split_dataset()` utility with train/val/test partitions and seed reproducibility.
- **Feature & Target Scaling:** `MinMaxScaler` and `StandardScaler` with robust `epsilon` handling and `inverse_transform` to convert model outputs back to physical units.
- **Universal Approximation Theorem:** Verified that a single hidden layer with non-linear activation reduces error by **96.6%** compared to a purely linear baseline.
- **Anti-Overfitting & Regularization Arsenal:**
  - **L2 Regularization (Ridge / Weight Decay):** Smooths weights via $dW += \lambda_2 W$.
  - **L1 Regularization (Lasso):** Induces sparsity via $dW += \lambda_1 \text{sign}(W)$, achieving **79.5% weight sparsity**.
  - **Inverted Dropout:** Applied during training with $1/(1-p)$ scaling to preserve signal expectation with zero test-time overhead.
  - **Early Stopping:** Monitored validation loss with configurable `patience` and automatic historical restoration of optimal weights (`restore_best_weights=True`).
- **Quantitative Evaluation Metrics:** Built a standalone evaluation module (`ANN/metrics.py`) providing MSE, RMSE, MAE, and $R^2$ Score.
- **Capstone Project (`TEST/motor_predictor.py`):** Real-world Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) rotational speed predictor.

### Capstone Project: PMSM Motor Speed Predictor

Using 20,000 real-world observations from an industrial PMSM motor, we trained a multi-layer regularized neural network to predict rotational speed (`motor_speed`, up to $6000\text{ RPM}$) using 6 electrical and thermal features (`u_q`, `u_d`, `i_q`, `i_d`, `ambient`, `coolant`).

```text
==================================================
REGRESSION REPORTS (PMSM MOTOR SPEED PREDICTOR)
==================================================
  MSE   : 9190.0576
  RMSE  : 95.8648 RPM
  MAE   : 39.6635 RPM
  R^2   : %99.74 (Skor: 0.9974)
==================================================
```

- **Accuracy:** Achieved an **$R^2$ score of 99.74%** and an average error of only **$39.66\text{ RPM}$** across the test set (< 0.7% relative error).
- **Efficiency:** Early Stopping terminated training at epoch 43 and restored the peak weights from **epoch 33** (`Val Loss: 0.001942`), saving over 57% of unnecessary training cycles.
- **Model Persistence:** Trained weights, biases, and normalization metrics are exported to `DATA/motor_model_weights.npz` using `np.savez()` for standalone inference.

![PMSM Motor Speed Prediction Results](DATA/motor_results.png)

> [!WARNING]
> Results may different between runs due to random weight initialization and dropout.

---

## Project Structure

├── ANN/                                # Chapter 1 & Core Engine
│   ├── activation_functions.py         # Sigmoid, ReLU, Leaky ReLU, Linear & derivatives
│   ├── basic_neural_training.py        # Neuron, Layer, NeuralNetwork (Dropout, L1/L2, Early Stopping)
│   ├── compare.py                      # Adam vs. SGD comparison experiment
│   ├── loss_functions.py               # MSE loss

│   ├── test_of_activation_func.py      # Activation function visualization

├── DATA/                               # Chapter 2: Data & Preprocessing

│   ├── scaler.py                       # MinMaxScaler & StandardScaler with inverse_transform
│   ├── motor_results.png               # PMSM final evaluation loss & prediction plot
│   ├── motor_model_weights.npz         # Exported weights, biases & scaler parameters
│   └── README.md                       # Chapter 2 progress report & documentation
├── TEST/                               # Chapter 2 Experiments & Capstone
│   ├── linear_vs_non-linear.py         # Linear model vs. hidden layer ANN
│   ├── overfitting.py                  # Overfitting sweet spot & L2 mitigation
│   ├── L1_vs_L2.py                     # Ridge vs. Lasso weight sparsity comparison
│   ├── dropout.py                      # Inverted dropout benchmark
│   ├── early_stopping.py               # Early stopping & best weight restoration
│   └── motor_predictor.py              # Chapter 2 Capstone: PMSM speed prediction

## Running the Code

## Key Features

- 🤖 AI-powered technical interviewer
- 💬 Dynamic follow-up questions

# InterviewIQ AI

> **Practice smarter. Interview with confidence.**

InterviewIQ AI is an AI-powered full-stack web application that simulates real technical job interviews. Instead of simply displaying interview questions, the platform creates an interactive interview experience where users answer questions, receive personalized AI feedback, and track their progress over time.

The project is designed as a capstone project for Holberton School and demonstrates modern software engineering practices, including frontend development, backend architecture, database management, authentication, AI integration, and deployment.

---

# Table of Contents

* [Overview](#overview)
* [Problem Statement](#problem-statement)
* [Solution](#solution)
* [Target Users](#target-users)
* [Features](#features)
* [Technology Stack](#technology-stack)
* [System Architecture](#system-architecture)
* [Project Structure](#project-structure)
* [Database Design](#database-design)
* [API Endpoints](#api-endpoints)
* [Security](#security)
* [Future Improvements](#future-improvements)
* [Installation](#installation)
* [Roadmap](#roadmap)
* [Contributors](#contributors)
* [License](#license)

---

# Overview

Preparing for technical interviews is one of the biggest challenges for aspiring software engineers. Most candidates practice by reading interview questions or watching online tutorials, but they rarely receive objective feedback about their answers.

InterviewIQ AI solves this problem by acting as an intelligent interviewer. Users participate in realistic mock interviews where AI evaluates their responses, identifies strengths and weaknesses, asks follow-up questions, and provides personalized recommendations for improvement.

The platform combines artificial intelligence with modern full-stack web technologies to create an engaging and practical interview preparation experience.

---

# Problem Statement

Traditional interview preparation methods have several limitations:

* No personalized feedback
* No realistic interview simulation
* Difficult to measure progress
* Limited opportunities to practice communication skills
* No adaptive follow-up questions

As a result, many candidates struggle during real interviews despite having sufficient technical knowledge.

---

# Solution

InterviewIQ AI provides an interactive AI-powered interview platform where users can:

* Practice technical interviews
* Receive instant AI feedback
* Track interview performance
* Improve weak technical areas
* Build confidence before real interviews

The platform is designed to simulate conversations with an experienced technical interviewer rather than simply displaying static questions.

---

# Target Users

### Primary Users

* Computer Science students
* Software Engineering students
* Bootcamp students
* Junior developers
* Internship applicants
* Career changers

### Secondary Users

* Universities
* Coding bootcamps
* Career centers
* Technical instructors

---

# Features

## User Authentication

* Register
* Login
* Logout
* Secure JWT authentication
* Password hashing

---

## Interview Categories

Users can choose different interview topics including:

* Frontend Development
* Backend Development
* Full Stack Development
* JavaScript
* React
* Node.js
* Python
* SQL
* DevOps
* System Design
* Behavioral Interviews

---

## Difficulty Levels

* Beginner
* Intermediate
* Advanced
* Senior

---

## AI Interview Session

Each interview follows a realistic workflow:

1. User selects category and difficulty
2. AI introduces the interview
3. AI asks a technical question
4. User submits an answer
5. AI evaluates the response
6. AI may ask follow-up questions
7. Final report is generated

---

## AI Feedback

Each answer receives detailed analysis including:

* Technical accuracy
* Completeness
* Communication quality
* Missing concepts
* Overall score
* Suggested improvements
* Example of a better answer

---

## Dashboard

Users can monitor their performance through:

* Interview history
* Average score
* Progress charts
* Strongest categories
* Weakest categories
* Recent activity

---

## Interview Reports

Each completed interview includes:

* Overall score
* Strengths
* Weaknesses
* AI recommendations
* Category breakdown
* Improvement suggestions

---

## Admin Panel

Administrators can:

* Add interview questions
* Edit questions
* Delete questions
* Manage users
* View platform statistics

---

## Technology Stack

This project is built using the MERN stack:

- **MongoDB:** Stores users, interview sessions, questions, answers, and AI feedback.
- **Express.js:** Provides REST API endpoints and handles backend business logic.
- **React:** Builds the interactive and responsive user interface.
- **Node.js:** Runs the backend server.

Additional technologies:

- Mongoose
- JWT
- bcrypt
- Google Gemini API
- Axios
- Tailwind CSS
- Chart.js

---

                REST API Requests

              Node.js + Express API
                      │
        Authentication & Business Logic
             │                    │

readme_content:
# EduPredict AI — Multi-Level Student Performance Prediction & Early Triage System

EduPredict AI is a production-grade academic decision-support platform designed to identify at-risk students weeks before examinations occur and provide personalized intervention roadmaps. The system supports learners across all educational tiers — from **Primary and Middle School** to **Secondary (Classes 9–10)**, **Higher Secondary / Intermediate (Classes 11–12)**, **Polytechnic Diploma**, **Undergraduate (B.Tech / B.E., B.Sc., BCA, B.Com, BA)**, and **Postgraduate (M.Tech, MBA, M.Sc., MCA)** degrees.

---

## 1. System Architecture Overview

EduPredict AI is structured as a full-stack, machine-learning-driven platform:
- **Responsive Frontend (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS)**: Preserves the Stitch AI design system, featuring an adaptive multi-step intake form with progressive guidance, real-time input validation, plain-English technical explanations, SHAP feature attribution bars, personalized study routines, and verified course recommendations.
- **Full-Stack Application Server (Node.js 22 + Express + Vite)**: Mounts all REST endpoints on port 3000 and serves client assets.
- **Persistent SQLite Data Layer (`data/edupredict.sqlite`)**: Database managed via SQL.js (WASM SQLite engine) ensuring zero data loss across reloads with schema migration and strict separation between verified user records and benchmark demo samples.
- **Machine Learning Core**: Calibrated supervised models (Random Forest v2.4 Ensemble, Decision Tree CART, and Logistic Regression L2) trained on documented datasets with prioritized At-Risk Recall (92.6%).
- **Standalone Python Service (`backend/`)**: Standalone FastAPI microservice (`backend/main.py`) with Pydantic validation, training pipeline (`backend/train_model.py`), documented datasets, and `requirements.txt`.

---

## 2. Multi-Level Education Coverage

The platform dynamically reconfigures forms, terminology, scaling factors, and course catalogues based on the selected education level:

| Education Level | Sub-Level Options | Streams / Branches Supported | Core Evaluated Indicators |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary School** (Classes 1–5) | Classes 1 to 5 | General Foundation | Term exam marks, homework completion, reading & activity practice hours, class attendance |
| **Middle School** (Classes 6–8) | Classes 6 to 8 | Core Curriculum | Midterm/annual marks, homework & periodic tests, self-study hours, class attendance |
| **Secondary School** (Classes 9–10) | Classes 9, 10 (Board) | General Board Curriculum | Pre-board/quarterly marks, internal assessment, science lab practicals, class attendance |
| **Higher Secondary / Intermediate** (Classes 11–12) | 1st Year (11th), 2nd Year (12th) | Science (PCM, PCB, PCMB), Commerce, Arts | Board marks, unit tests, science lab practicals, competitive entrance exam prep (JEE, NEET, CUET) |
| **Polytechnic Diploma** | Semesters 1 to 6 | Mechanical, CS, EEE, Civil, Auto, ECE | Previous semester %, sessional & midterms, workshop & lab practicals, attendance |
| **Undergraduate B.Tech / B.E.** | Semesters 1 to 8 (Years 1–4) | CSE, AI & Data Science, IT, ECE, EEE, ME, Civil | Cumulative CGPA, Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE), lab practicals, attendance |
| **Undergraduate B.Sc. / BCA / B.Com / BA** | Semesters 1 to 6 | BCA, B.Sc. CS, Mathematics, Finance, BBA, BA | Prior semester marks, continuous internal assessment, assignment completion, attendance |
| **Postgraduate M.Tech / M.E.** | Semesters 1 to 4 | AI & ML, VLSI, CSE, Power Systems, Thermal, Cyber | Postgraduate CGPA, coursework exams, seminars & papers, thesis research progress |
| **Postgraduate M.Sc. / MCA / MBA** | Semesters 1 to 4 | MCA, MBA (Finance/Marketing/HR), M.Sc. Data Sci | Prior term GPA, case studies, capstone project progress, seminar evaluations |
| **Other Programs** | Phases 1 to 3 | Software, Data, Trades, General | Recent assessments, continuous coursework marks, weekly study dedication |

---

## 3. Real-World Datasets and Data Quality

The machine learning models are trained and calibrated on documented real-world datasets:
1. **UCI Student Performance Dataset (Cortez & Silva, 2008)**:
   - Source: University of Minho / UCI Machine Learning Repository.
   - Sample Count: 1,044 secondary school student records (Portuguese & Mathematics cohorts).
   - Features: Prior evaluation periods ($G_1$ & $G_2$), school absences, weekly study time, past failures.
   - Representation: School and higher secondary students.
2. **Higher Education Engineering & Collegiate Academic Cohort Benchmark**:
   - Sample Count: 1,500 collegiate student records (1,200 training, 300 held-out test split).
   - Features: Lecture attendance, continuous assignment scores, weekly study hours, prerequisite GPA, laboratory practical marks.
   - Representation: Diploma, undergraduate engineering, and postgraduate coursework cohorts.

---

## 4. Model Evaluation & Explainability

All metrics are evaluated using a 10-fold stratified cross-validation split:

| Architecture | Overall Accuracy | At-Risk Recall | Macro Precision | Weighted F1 | Multi-Class AUC | Status |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Random Forest v2.4 (Ensemble)** | **89.4%** | **92.6%** | **88.1%** | **90.3%** | **0.942** | **Selected (Production)** |
| Decision Tree (CART) | 83.2% | 84.1% | 82.5% | 83.1% | 0.865 | Interpretable Baseline |
| Logistic Regression (L2) | 81.7% | 80.5% | 81.2% | 80.8% | 0.851 | Linear Baseline |

### Metric Meanings in Simple English
- **Overall Accuracy (89.4%)**: Roughly 89 out of every 100 students had their exact performance tier predicted correctly.
- **At-Risk Recall (92.6%)**: Out of 100 students who were truly at risk of failing, the model successfully identified over 92 of them. This is prioritized to eliminate dangerous false negatives.
- **Macro Precision (88.1%)**: Measures the reliability of each risk flag across all categories equally, ensuring small groups get equal importance.
- **Weighted F1-Score (90.3%)**: Harmonic balance between precision and recall, adjusted for class sizes.

---

## 5. Verified Level-Based Course Catalogue

Course recommendations match the student's exact education level, stream, and identified weaknesses. Every course links to official pages from verified providers:
- **Khan Academy**: Early Math, Pre-Algebra, High School Science, Class 9 & 10 Mathematics, Calculus 1, College Statistics.
- **SWAYAM / NCERT**: Senior Secondary Physics, Higher Secondary Accountancy, Secondary English Communication.
- **NPTEL (IITs & IISc)**: Basic Electrical Technology (IIT KGP), Engineering Mechanics (IIT Madras), Data Structures & Algorithms in Python (IIT Madras), Database Management Systems (IIT KGP), Deep Learning (IIT Madras), Research Methodology (IIT Madras).
- **Cisco Networking Academy**: Python Essentials 1, Computer Hardware Basics, Introduction to Cybersecurity.
- **Microsoft Learn**: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900 Learning Path).
- **IBM SkillsBuild**: Machine Learning & AI Foundations.
- **Coursera (Stanford / Wharton / UMich)**: Machine Learning Specialization, Business Foundations, Python for Everybody.
- **edX (Harvard / MITx)**: CS50’s Artificial Intelligence with Python, MIT Introduction to Computational Thinking and Data Science.

---

## 6. Actionable Personalized Study Plan

Every prediction generates an actionable study plan:
- **Primary Goal**: Immediate syllabus pacing recovery (for At-Risk) or distinction preparation.
- **Recommended Study Time**: Calculated weekly targets (e.g., 14–18 hours/week, 2 hours daily).
- **Daily Routine**: Structured 45-minute focused blocks with 10-minute active recall breaks.
- **Revision Strategy**: Spaced repetition with self-tests every weekend.
- **Assignment Action**: Submitting assignments 24 hours before deadlines to review corrections.
- **Next Assessment Target**: Numerical score goal for the upcoming evaluation.

---

## 7. Responsiveness & Tested Viewports

The user interface has been engineered and verified across desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints:
- **Small Mobile**: 320 × 568 (iPhone SE 1st gen), 360 × 800 (Android Standard), 375 × 812 (iPhone X/11 Pro)
- **Modern Mobile**: 390 × 844 (iPhone 12/13/14), 430 × 932 (iPhone Pro Max)
- **Tablet**: 768 × 1024 (iPad Portrait), 1024 × 768 (iPad Landscape)
- **Laptop & Desktop**: 1366 × 768 (Laptop), 1440 × 900 (Desktop Baseline)

Key responsive safeguards:
- Forms automatically stack vertically on screens $< 640\text{px}$.
- Touch targets $\ge 44\text{px}$ on mobile screens.
- Zero horizontal window overflow; tables use smooth container scrolling with responsive text truncation.
- Persistent sidebar automatically collapses into a touch-friendly slide drawer on mobile screens.
- Modal dialogs feature responsive max-height scrolling (`max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto`).

---

## 8. Development & Execution Instructions

```bash
# 1. Install Node.js dependencies
npm install

# 2. Start full-stack development server (Express + Vite on port 3000)
npm run dev

# 3. Optional: Run Python training pipeline & FastAPI standalone service
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
python backend/train_model.py
uvicorn backend.main:app --port 8000 --reload
```

# devops-capstone-project [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![Python 3.9](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.9-green.svg)](https://shields.io/) This repository contains the starter code for the project in [**IBM-CD0285EN-SkillsNetwork DevOps Capstone Project**](https://www.coursera.org/learn/devops-capstone-project?specialization=devops-and-software-engineering) which is part of the [**IBM DevOps and Software Engineering Professional Certificate**](https://www.coursera.org/professional-certificates/devops-and-software-engineering) ## Usage You should use this template to start your DevOps Capstone project. It contains all of the code that you will need to get started. Do Not fork this code! It is meant to be used by pressing the **Use this Template** button in GitHub. This will copy the code to your own repository with no connection back to the original repository like a fork would. This is what you want. ## Development Environment These labs are designed to be executed in the IBM Developer Skills Network Cloud IDE with OpenShift. Please use the links provided in the Coursera Capstone project to access the lab environment. Once you are in the lab environment, you can initialize it with `bin/setup.sh` by sourcing it. (*Note: DO NOT run this program as a bash script. It sets environment variable and so must be sourced*): ```bash source bin/setup.sh ``` This will install Python 3.9, make it the default, modify the bash prompt, create a Python virtual environment and activate it. After sourcing it you prompt should look like this: ```bash (venv) theia:project$ ``` ## Useful commands Under normal circumstances you should not have to run these commands. They are performed automatically at setup but may be useful when things go wrong: ### Activate the Python 3.9 virtual environment You can activate the Python 3.9 environment with: ```bash source ~/venv/bin/activate ``` ### Installing Python dependencies These dependencies are installed as part of the setup process but should you need to install them again, first make sure that the Python 3.9 virtual environment is activated and then use the `make install` command: ```bash make install ``` ### Starting the Postgres Docker container The labs use Postgres running in a Docker container. If for some reason the service is not available you can start it with: ```bash make db ``` You can use the `docker ps` command to make sure that postgres is up and running. ## Project layout The code for the microservice is contained in the `service` package. All of the test are in the `tests` folder. The code follows the **Model-View-Controller** pattern with all of the database code and business logic in the model (`models.py`), and all of the RESTful routing on the controller (`routes.py`). ```text ├── service <- microservice package │   ├── common/ <- common log and error handlers │   ├── config.py <- Flask configuration object │   ├── models.py <- code for the persistent model │   └── routes.py <- code for the REST API routes ├── setup.cfg <- tools setup config └── tests <- folder for all of the tests ├── factories.py <- test factories ├── test_cli_commands.py <- CLI tests ├── test_models.py <- model unit tests └── test_routes.py <- route unit tests ``` ## Data Model The Account model contains the following fields: | Name | Type | Optional | |------|------|----------| | id | Integer| False | | name | String(64) | False | | email | String(64) | False | | address | String(256) | False | | phone_number | String(32) | True | | date_joined | Date | False | ## Your Task Complete this microservice by implementing REST API's for `READ`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `LIST` while maintaining **95%** code coverage. In true **Test Driven Development** fashion, first write tests for the code you "wish you had", and then write the code to make them pass. ## Local Kubernetes Development This repo can also be used for local Kubernetes development. It is not advised that you run these commands in the Cloud IDE environment. The purpose of these commands are to simulate the Cloud IDE environment locally on your computer. At a minimum, you will need [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop) installed on your computer. For the full development environment, you will also need [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com) with the [Remote Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers) extension from the Visual Studio Marketplace. All of these can be installed manually by clicking on the links above or you can use a package manager like **Homebrew** on Mac of **Chocolatey** on Windows. Please only use these commands for working stand-alone on your own computer with the VSCode Remote Container environment provided. 1. Bring up a local K3D Kubernetes cluster ```bash $ make cluster ``` 2. Install Tekton ```bash $ make tekton ``` 3. Install the ClusterTasks that the Cloud IDE has ```bash $ make clustertasks ``` You can now perform Tekton development locally, just like in the Cloud IDE lab environment. ## Author [John Rofrano](https://www.coursera.org/instructor/johnrofrano), Senior Technical Staff Member, DevOps Champion, @ IBM Research, and Instructor @ Coursera ## License Licensed under the Apache License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) ##

readme_content:
# CTRL + ALT + DEFEAT — LAST CITY

A post-apocalyptic city-building strategy game that runs entirely in the
browser. Gather Salvage from the ruins, lay out a settlement by hand, put
survivors to work, research lost technology, and hold the perimeter when the
raids come.

No build step, no framework, no package install. It is HTML, CSS and
JavaScript, and it runs from any static host including GitHub Pages.

---

## Running the game

### The quickest way

Open `index.html` in a modern browser. Everything works except cloud saves,
which need a real `http(s)` origin.

### The way that matches production

Serve the folder over HTTP. Any of these will do:

```bash
# Python 3 (installed on macOS and most Linux systems)
python3 -m http.server 8000

# Node
npx serve .
```

Then open <http://localhost:8000>.

A real origin matters because browsers treat `file://` as a special case:
`localStorage` and the account system behave differently there. If you are
testing saving or logging in, use the HTTP route.

### On GitHub Pages

Push the contents of this folder to a repository and enable Pages. See
**INSTALL.md** for step-by-step instructions written for a first-time user.

---

## What you do in the game

### The five zones

Progress runs through five zones, each with its own currency, its own activity
and its own permanent upgrades:

| Zone | Name | Currency | What you do there |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Ashfall Outpost | Salvage | Gather, build, restore the beacon |
| 02 | Overgrown Depot | Scrap | Search sites for keys and supplies |
| 03 | Copperworks Foundry | Parts | Assemble engines to a changing recipe |
| 04 | Neon Relay | Circuits | Harvest energy from the field |
| 05 | Celestial Citadel | Cores | Break the Guardian's shields and fire |

### The tabs

* **Play** — the original zone activity for whichever zone you are in.
* **City** — the interactive settlement. Drag buildings onto plots, lay roads,
  assign jobs, repair damage, open new districts.
* **Defense** — real-time lane battles against incoming waves.
* **Research** — a branching technology tree across five eras.
* **Upgrades** — buildings, tools and permanent research, as before.
* **Glyphs** — permanent collection buffs, as before.
* **Pets** — hatch, equip and merge companions, plus levelling, equipment,
  training and roles.
* **Stories** — the recovered transmissions archive.
* **Stats** — lifetime records and achievements.

---

## The city

The City tab is an isometric settlement you lay out yourself.

* **Place a building** — drag it from the build tray onto a lit plot, or tap
  the tray entry and then tap the map. Buildings you already own are free to
  place; you are only charged when you need to buy a new one, and that
  purchase goes through the game's own pricing.
* **Pick one up** — clearing an original building returns it to the tray. You
  never lose a building you paid for by rearranging your city.
* **Roads** — the Roads tool lays and removes them. Roads speed citizens up
  and give a small efficiency bonus.
* **Jobs** — survivors arrive as your Population grows. Assign them to posts
  that your buildings provide, or press Auto-assign.
* **Services** — power, food and security come from what you build. A
  brownout or a food shortage lowers city efficiency, which feeds back into
  production. A well-run city helps; a neglected one costs you.
* **Districts** — the map opens outward as you unlock zones.
* **Camera** — drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, arrow keys to move,
  `+`/`-` to zoom, `Home` to recentre.
* **Search the ruins** — wreckage, crates and old terminals are scattered
  across the map. With the Inspect tool, tap one to recover Salvage, research
  points or a piece of the story.

---

## Defense

Waves advance down three lanes toward your core.

* A **charge** meter refills over time; each card costs charge.
* Tap a card, then tap a lane to deploy there.
* **Melee** units cannot reach fliers. **Siege** units walk past defenders and
  go for towers. **Support** units heal whoever is in front of them.
* Your towers are the turrets and barricades you actually built in the City
  tab, so a defended settlement fights better.
* Every fifth wave is a boss with an ability of its own.
* Lose, and the wave damages real structures, which you repair for Salvage.

First clears pay full rewards once. Replays pay a reduced amount, so a wave is
practice rather than a farm.

---

## Research

Twenty-four technologies across five eras, with prerequisites. Research points
come from Research Labs you build in the city and from caches you find in the
ruins. Banked points flow into whichever project is active.

Research is permanent: it survives every reset, including a City Renewal.

---

## Companions

The existing collection, hatching, merging and zone multipliers are unchanged.
On top of them:

* **Levels** earned by playing, with six abilities unlocked along the way.
* **Equipment** in three slots, found through training, missions and discoveries.
* **Training** sessions on a timer.
* **Care** — feeding and play build a bond.
* **Roles** — one companion can help the city, one can scout, one can fight.

Open it from the button at the bottom of the Pets tab.

---

## People and missions

Named survivors turn up as the settlement grows. Conversations branch, and
your answers are recorded permanently — they change what each character offers
you later and what missions open up.

Exploration missions run in real time with a success chance you can improve by
growing your roster, training your crews, researching, and assigning a scout
companion.

City events interrupt occasionally with a decision that costs or pays something
real.

---

## Settings

Under **⚙ Settings** in the header:

* Sound, ambient audio, effects and story popups (original controls).
* Music on/off, with separate music and effects volume sliders.
* Weather, day/night, citizens and screen shake.
* Detail level — Automatic, High, Medium or Low. Automatic samples the device
  once and lowers particle counts on a small or low-core machine.
* Replay the opening cinematic.

Your operating system's **reduced-motion** setting always wins. With it on, the
cinematic becomes a readable storyboard you page through, the city stops
animating and draws on demand, and decorative motion is switched off.

---

## Saving

* **Guest play** saves to this browser's `localStorage`.
* **An account** adds cloud saves through Supabase, including Google sign-in.
* Saves from the previous build load with nothing lost. See CHANGES.md for how
  that is guaranteed and TEST_RESULTS.md for how it was verified.

---

## Project layout

```
index.html              the game
src/
  game/
    game.js             core loop, economy, saves  (original)
    economy.js          upgrade curves             (original)
    progression.js      zone projects              (original)
    adventure.js        zones and companions       (original)
    pets.js             hatching and merging       (original)
    glyphs.js           glyph collections          (original)
    migration.js        new-state schema + save migration      (new)
    audio.js            music and sound engine                 (new)
    citybuilder.js      the interactive city                   (new)
    cinematic.js        the opening sequence                   (new)
    combat.js           lane battles                           (new)
    research.js         the technology tree                    (new)
    events.js           NPCs, missions, city events            (new)
    companions-plus.js  companion levels and equipment         (new)
  ui/
    expansion.js        the layer that joins new to old        (new)
    world.js, player-ui.js, terminal.js, effects.js,
    startup.js, feedback.js                        (original)
  cloud/
    cloud-config.js     public Supabase config     (original)
    cloud-save.js       accounts and cloud saves   (original)
  styles/               stylesheets, original and new
assets/                 zone and companion artwork (WebP)
supabase/               SQL for the cloud-save backend
tests/                  the automated test suite
```

---

## Tests

```bash
node tests/run.js              # everything available
node tests/run.js --no-browser # static and unit tests only
```

The static and unit suites are dependency-free and run on a clean checkout.
The browser suite needs Playwright, and reports as skipped without it:

```bash
npm install --no-save playwright
node tests/run.js
```

See TEST_RESULTS.md for the most recent run and for what is deliberately not
covered.

---

## Credits

Created by **CTRL + ALT + DEFEAT** · IT 485 Capstone Project.

Zone illustrations and companion portraits are the project's own AI-generated
artwork. Everything drawn in the city, the battle arena and the opening
cinematic is generated procedurally in code — there are no sprite sheets. All
music and sound effects are synthesised in the browser with the Web Audio API;
no audio files are downloaded and no external audio service is used.

readme_content:
# 🍽️ BusinessLaunch AI — Should I open a restaurant or café here?

**NTI Machine Learning & Data Analysis Track · Final Capstone Project**

BusinessLaunch AI helps an entrepreneur evaluate a location in **Philadelphia, PA** before opening a restaurant or café. It combines regression, NLP, clustering and simulation on the [Yelp Open Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/yelp-dataset/yelp-dataset) into one Streamlit app that answers:

> *"If a businessman opens a new restaurant or café at this location, what **opportunities**, **competition**, **customer expectations** and **financial risks** could they face?"*

## Why it matters
Restaurants are among the riskiest small businesses to open: in this very dataset only **61% of Philadelphia restaurants and cafés are still open** at the snapshot. Common causes (wrong location, underestimated competition, misread customer expectations, unrealistic costs) are visible in public data **before** signing a lease, but owners rarely have the tools to read that data. BusinessLaunch AI turns 14,570 businesses, ~700k reviews and 1.29M check-ins (2010–2022) into a location report a non-technical owner can use.

## What the app does
| Page | Question answered | Team member · method |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · Location Intelligence** | How much competition is there, and how popular could a new restaurant here become? | Member 1 · haversine BallTree features, Linear Regression / Random Forest / Gradient Boosting / **HistGradientBoosting** |
| **2 · Customer Reviews** | What do customers of nearby competitors praise and complain about? | Member 2 · TF-IDF + **Logistic Regression** / Naive Bayes sentiment, **NMF** complaint topics |
| **3 · Market Clusters** | What kind of market environment is this? | Member 3 · neighbourhood profiles, **K-Means** vs Agglomerative (Ward) vs Gaussian Mixture |
| **4 · Financial Simulator** | Do the numbers work, and how risky are they? | Member 3 · break-even, scenarios, **Monte Carlo** (4,000 runs), sensitivity |
| **🎮 Beat the AI** | Can your instincts beat the models? | Three games on real data: *Higher or Lower* (vs the Member 1 regression), *Complaint Detective* (vs the NMF topic model), *Pick the Spot* (vs the Member 3 risk scores), with points, streaks and badges |
| **5 · Launch Report** | Go / caution / high risk — and why? | All · explainable percentile scores, rules, alternative locations, downloadable report, **comparison of saved locations** |

![Market environments](docs/images/m3_cluster_map.png)

## Results
| Component | Model selected | Key result (held-out data) | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Popularity regression (Member 1) | HistGradientBoosting, log target | **Test R² 0.61**, MAE 51.3 reviews | median baseline MAE 99.4 (−48%) |
| Sentiment classification (Member 2) | TF-IDF (1–2 grams) + Logistic Regression (C = 10) | **Test macro F1 0.944**, accuracy 0.964 | majority class 0.796 |
| Market clustering (Member 3) | StandardScaler + K-Means, k = 4 | silhouette 0.23 (best of 3 methods), bootstrap ARI 0.87 | Ward 0.17, GMM 0.17 |

Highlights
* **Leakage-safe evaluation.** Member 1 splits by ~1 km spatial blocks and Member 2 by business, so test restaurants were never seen in training. Leakage assertions (target perturbation, fold-local vocabularies, train-only imputation) all pass.
* **Feature engineering beat model choice.** Adding Yelp attributes, opening hours, a business-age proxy and nearby check-in activity raised the regression from R² 0.06 (location only) to 0.61.
* **Four market environments** emerge without coordinates as inputs: *Downtown hub* (high demand, intense competition, 56% still open), *Busy outer corridor* (strong demand, weak competitors: the best opportunity/risk balance), *Mixed neighbourhood market* and *Quiet residential*.
* **The risk score is back-tested on real outcomes.** Among 2,803 restaurants and cafés that opened in 2012–2019, 27% closed in low-risk areas vs 45% in high-risk areas (AUC 0.60). High-*demand* areas close *more* often, so the verdict always weighs opportunity against risk.
* **Robustness checks.** A 20-configuration random search and a Poisson loss did not beat the selected regression. The popularity estimate comes with a conformally calibrated 80% range, and the clusters survive changing the radius to 1.5 km (ARI 0.60).
* **Six complaint themes** from 127k negative reviews: service & staff attitude, food taste & quality, wait times & table service, orders/delivery/phone, cheesesteaks & sandwiches, pizza quality.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ![](docs/images/m1_observed_vs_estimated.png) | ![](docs/images/m2_confusion_matrix.png) | ![](docs/images/m3_finance.png) |

## Repository structure
```
BusinessLaunchAI/
├── app/                         Streamlit application
│   ├── Home.py                  entry point + grouped navigation (streamlit run app/Home.py)
│   ├── common.py                shared loaders, sidebar location picker, saved locations
│   ├── ui.py                    design system: CSS, headers, cards, game points
│   ├── views/                   home, location, reviews, clusters, finance, report, games
│   └── saved_locations.json     saved locations (3 demo locations included)
├── .streamlit/config.toml       app theme (colours, fonts, chart palette)
├── run_app.bat                  double-click launcher for Windows
├── src/businesslaunch/          reusable, tested Python package
│   ├── data.py                  streaming Yelp JSON / ZIP readers
│   ├── location.py              Member 1 features for a hypothetical restaurant + model wrapper
│   ├── competitor_analysis.py   Member 2 competitor review analysis
│   ├── market.py                Member 3 neighbourhood profiles, concept gaps
│   ├── finance.py               Member 3 simulator (projection, scenarios, Monte Carlo)
│   └── recommend.py             Member 3 explainable recommendation
├── notebooks/
│   └── BusinessLaunchAI_ML_Pipeline.ipynb   the complete ML work in one notebook (Parts 1–3)
├── outputs/member1|member2|member3/   trained models, metrics, figures, CSVs used by the app
├── tests/                       unit tests + app smoke test
├── data/                        Yelp files go here (not committed, see data/README.md)
├── docs/                        architecture, presentation outline, images
└── requirements.txt
```

## Setup
Requires Python 3.11.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/BelalOsaKa/BusinessLaunchAI.git
cd BusinessLaunchAI
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate            # Windows  (macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate)
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Run the app (no dataset download needed)
The trained models and exported tables in `outputs/` are committed, so the app runs straight away. Run it **from the project root** so the theme in `.streamlit/config.toml` is applied:
```bash
streamlit run app/Home.py
```
On Windows you can also double-click `run_app.bat`.
Open http://localhost:8501, choose an area (or type coordinates) in the sidebar and go through the five pages. Use **💾 Save location** in the sidebar and **Save these assumptions** on the Financial Simulator page; the Launch Report then uses your numbers and compares all saved locations. Three demo locations are pre-saved in `app/saved_locations.json`. After changing any code, stop and restart the app (Streamlit keeps shared modules in memory).

### Reproduce the models
1. Download the Yelp Open Dataset and place the files in `data/` (see [data/README.md](data/README.md)).
2. Open `notebooks/BusinessLaunchAI_ML_Pipeline.ipynb` and *Run All*: Part 1 (≈5 min) → Part 2 (needs the 5 GB review file, ≈20–40 min; skip it if you don't have the file, Part 3 reads its saved results) → Part 3 (≈3 min). Each part writes to `outputs/memberN/`.
3. Run the tests: `python -m pytest tests` (or `python tests/test_core.py` and `python tests/test_app_pages.py`).

## Methodology in brief
**Data.** Philadelphia, PA businesses (14,570 after cleaning). The restaurant/café universe is 6,174 businesses (5,855 tagged `Restaurants` plus 319 cafés/coffee shops). There are 703,584 cleaned reviews and 1.29M check-ins, with the snapshot ending January 2022.

**Member 1 — regression.** The target is cumulative `review_count`, a popularity proxy (log-transformed). Features include competitor counts within 0.5/1/2 km, open competitors, density, distance to City Hall, own rating and price, 13 service attributes, alcohol/noise/Wi-Fi/parking, opening hours, years since first check-in, nearby check-in activity and 20 category tags. The model is selected by 3-fold spatial CV on training blocks, then validation MAE. Each restaurant's own check-in count is excluded because it duplicates the target.

**Member 2 — NLP.** Labels come from stars (1–2 negative, 4–5 positive; 3 excluded from training). Text is lowercased with negation preserved ("don't" → "do not"), then vectorised with TF-IDF (unigrams + bigrams). Models are tuned with GroupKFold by business and selected on validation macro F1. NMF on negative reviews produces the complaint topics, which are aggregated per business and per location.

**Member 3 — clustering, finance, recommendation.** 611 grid areas (0.5 km cells) are each profiled with 13 features within 1 km: supply, survival, concept mix, price, rating, % negative reviews, demand, diversity and complaint mix. The pipeline is median-impute → StandardScaler → clustering, with k chosen by a pre-stated rule: k ≥ 4, bootstrap ARI ≥ 0.8, smallest cluster ≥ 5%, then the highest silhouette. Opportunity and risk scores are percentiles against all areas. The financial model is driven by user assumptions; data informs only the default ticket (local price level) and a bounded ±40% traffic adjustment (local demand percentile). A Monte Carlo simulation gives the probability of payback within 24 months.

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the data flow between members.

## Limitations
* Review count measures **popularity on Yelp, not revenue**. Yelp has no sales, rent or cost data, so all money figures are user assumptions.
* The data is a single January 2022 snapshot. Closure dates are unknown, and older businesses have had more time to collect reviews (handled with the business-age feature).
* Aspect sentiment uses a keyword lexicon and a sentence-level classifier trained on whole reviews, so very short sentences ("a bit expensive though") can be misread.
* A transformer model (DistilBERT) was not trained: it needs the 5 GB review file and a GPU; this machine has 8 GB RAM and no GPU.
* Sentiment labels come from star ratings: sarcasm and mixed reviews are the main source of errors, and the 2★/4★ boundaries are hardest.
* Neighbourhood circles overlap, so clusters describe tendencies (silhouette 0.23). The opportunity/risk weights are transparent rules, not learned from outcomes.
* Only Philadelphia city limits are covered, so competitors just across the city boundary are missed.

## Future work
* Validate recommendations against restaurants that opened after the snapshot (city business-licence data).
* Add census income, foot traffic and rent data to replace financial assumptions with local estimates.
* Use dated reviews for trend features ("is this area getting better?") and fine-tune a transformer (e.g. DistilBERT) for aspect-level sentiment.
* Deploy to Streamlit Community Cloud and add an LLM summary of competitor reviews.

## Team
| Member | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Member 1 | Location intelligence & regression (business + check-in data) |
| Member 2 | NLP, sentiment classification & complaint topics (review data) |
| Member 3 | Clustering, financial simulation, recommendation & app integration |

GitHub: [@BelalOsaKa](https://github.com/BelalOsaKa) · [@SeifTdec](https://github.com/SeifTdec) · [@ezzat2803-crypto](https://github.com/ezzat2803-crypto)

*Data: Yelp Open Dataset, used under the Yelp Dataset Terms of Use for academic purposes.*
