description: A social app where travelers and photographers discover hyper-local, community-verified photo spots and connect with other travelers/photographers.
readme_content:
# Wanderlens

A social discovery app for travelers and photographers, built with Expo and
React Native as an MCA capstone project.

Most travel apps put an AI concierge at the center and treat the social side
as an afterthought. **Wanderlens does the opposite: community and connection
are the product, and AI is a supporting feature.** It rests on three pillars:

1. **A crowdsourced photo-spot map.** Real photographers post geo-tagged
   spots with tips. Nothing on the map is AI-generated.
2. **A connection layer.** Meet travelers and photographers by shared
   destination, dates or genre. Connections are mutual and agreed by both
   sides; there are no followers and no follower counts.
3. **Lightweight AI grounded in the app's own data.** A trail generator that
   sequences *real community spots* into a photo outing, and a caption
   assistant. It is not a general chatbot.

[`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md) lists what is built and what was deliberately
deferred.

---

## Features

### Discover
- **Feed**: a golden-hour/blue-hour countdown for your location, a "Spots
  near you" strip, a "Photographers who've shot nearby" strip, and a
  vertical feed with genre and time-of-day filters.
- **Map**: every spot in the area on screen, loaded as you pan and zoom, with
  pins that group spots a few metres apart. Tap a pin for a card with the
  photo and tips.
- **Spot detail**: photo, tips, likes, saves, threaded comments (edit and
  delete your own), sharing, and "View on map".

### Share
- **Add a spot** with its location from GPS, a place search, or by tapping
  the map. Location lookups fall back to OpenStreetMap when the phone's
  geocoder fails, which it does for disputed regions such as Arunachal
  Pradesh.
- **Geo-tag camera**: shoot in the app to record coordinates, altitude, the
  place name and address, and the current weather, and save a "stamped" copy
  with that information to your gallery.
- **Photo styles**: frames such as Polaroid, Film Retro, Vintage, Noir,
  Golden Hour and Blue Hour, with an optional caption. Use them on a new
  post, or in a standalone studio that saves the result to your gallery.
- **AI caption suggestions** for a new post.

### Connect
- **Discover people** by genre, or by **trip matching**: people whose planned
  trip shares a destination and overlapping dates with yours.
- **Mutual connections**: send, accept, decline, cancel and remove requests.
- **Public profiles** with each person's spots, and block and report.

### Chat
- 1:1 and group chats with photos, photo galleries, video, voice notes,
  documents, and shared locations and spots.
- Replies, reactions, read receipts, typing indicators, message search,
  archiving, and message requests from people you aren't connected to.
- Group management: name, photo, description, members and admins.

### Plan
- **AI photo trail**: pick a genre and a number of stops (3 to 6), and the AI
  orders real nearby spots into an outing with a tip for each stop. Save the
  trails you like to **My trails**.
- **Notes**: private notes, which can be linked to a spot.
- **Saved spots**: your bookmarked spots.

### Account
- Email/password sign-up with a live username check, onboarding, and
  forgot-password through an email deep link.
- An in-app **notification bell** for connection requests, likes, comments,
  replies, shares and message requests.
- A **first-run tour** that highlights the key controls, and can be replayed
  from the Profile menu.
- **Account deletion** that removes personal data and anonymizes the profile
  to "Deleted user", so spots stay on the map for the community.

---

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Expo SDK 54, React Native 0.81.5, React 19.1 |
| Language | TypeScript, `strict: true` |
| Routing | Expo Router 6 (file-based, `app/`) |
| Backend | Supabase: Postgres + PostGIS, Auth, Storage, Realtime, Edge Functions (Deno). Row Level Security on every table |
| State | React Context for auth, chat and notifications; Zustand to pass values between screens; each screen fetches its own server data |
| Maps | `@maplibre/maplibre-react-native` with free [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org) tiles |
| Geocoding | `expo-location`, with [Nominatim](https://nominatim.org) (OpenStreetMap) as a fallback |
| AI | Groq `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (trails), Gemini `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (captions), both called only from Edge Functions |
| Other APIs | [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com) (weather), [sunrise-sunset.org](https://sunrise-sunset.org) (golden hour) |
| Animation | `react-native-reanimated` 4 + `react-native-worklets` |
| Error monitoring | `@sentry/react-native` (off in development) |

Every external service is free or on a free tier. That was a project
constraint, and it is why the map uses MapLibre and not `react-native-maps`,
which needs a billed Google Maps key even for non-Google tiles.

**Design.** The app has one dark "golden hour / blue hour" theme on purpose.
It does not follow the phone's light/dark setting. Colors, fonts and radii
all come from `constants/theme.ts`.

---

## Getting started

> **Expo Go cannot run this app.** It uses `expo-dev-client` and a native map
> module (MapLibre) that Expo Go doesn't include, so you need a development
> build.

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 20.19.4 or newer (React Native 0.81 requires it), and npm
- Android: Android Studio with an SDK and an emulator or device. iOS: Xcode
  (macOS only). Or build in the cloud with EAS (`eas.json` is included).
- A Supabase project (the free tier is enough). See [Backend setup](#backend-setup).

### Install and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/devKiNGCRiC/wanderlens.git
cd wanderlens
npm install
```

Create a `.env` file in the project root:

```
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=your_supabase_url
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_supabase_anon_key
EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=your_sentry_dsn   # optional
```

`EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values are compiled into the app and can be read by anyone
who has it. Only put public values here. The anon key is safe because Row
Level Security protects every table. **The AI keys do not go in `.env`.**
They are Supabase secrets (see below).

Build and install the development app once, then start the dev server:

```bash
npm run android      # or: npm run ios   (compiles the development app)
npm start            # afterwards: live reload for JavaScript changes
```

You only need to rebuild after adding a native dependency or changing a
config plugin in `app.config.js`.

### Backend setup

> **Known gap:** `supabase/migrations/` does **not** hold the full schema yet.
> The core tables (`profiles`, `spots`, `spot_likes`, `spot_comments`,
> `comment_likes`, `saved_spots`, `connections`, `trails`) and the older RPCs
> (`feed_spots`, `nearby_spots`, `discover_people`, `get_spot`,
> `get_spot_comments`, `get_saved_spots`, `get_connection_status`,
> `handle_new_user`) were created in the Supabase dashboard before migrations
> were tracked. The migrations cover everything added after that: chat,
> notifications, AI quotas, account deletion, trips, geo-tags, notes, and
> `nearby_photographers`. Setting up a fresh project from this repo alone is
> not possible yet.

On the existing project:

1. Apply new migration files **by hand** in the Supabase SQL Editor, in
   filename order. Don't use `supabase db push`: the remote migration
   history is empty, so it would try to replay every migration and fail on
   objects that already exist. If the app then reports a missing column,
   run `notify pgrst, 'reload schema';` so the API picks up the change.
2. Link the CLI: `supabase login`, then `supabase link --project-ref <your-ref>`.
3. Set the AI secrets:
   ```bash
   supabase secrets set GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_key GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_key
   ```
4. Deploy the Edge Functions:
   ```bash
   supabase functions deploy generate-trail generate-caption delete-account
   ```
   `delete-account` needs no extra secret. It uses the service-role key that
   Supabase gives every Edge Function.
5. In **Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs**, add
   `wanderlens://reset-password` so the password-reset email link opens the
   app.

---

## How it works

### Navigation and auth gating
Every file in `app/` is a route. `(auth)` and `(tabs)` are route groups (the
parentheses don't appear in the URL), and `[id].tsx` files are dynamic
routes. Access control lives in one place, `app/_layout.tsx`, which has four
`<Stack.Protected>` blocks:

1. Password recovery in progress: only the reset-password screen
2. Signed in and onboarded: the whole app
3. Signed in, not onboarded: only onboarding
4. Signed out: login, sign-up and forgot-password

Exactly one block is active at a time. When the user signs in or out, the
router moves them automatically. **A new screen must be registered inside
the right block,** or it can be reached regardless of whether the user is
signed in.

### Data
- **Reads go through RPCs** (Postgres functions such as `feed_spots` and
  `nearby_spots`) that return joined data in one request. **Writes go
  straight to tables.**
- **Row Level Security is the security boundary.** The client is not trusted.
- Screens reload with `useFocusEffect` each time they come into view, so
  data is never stale after navigating back.
- Chat uses Supabase Realtime for new messages, read receipts and typing
  indicators.

### AI
The app calls Supabase Edge Functions (`generate-trail`, `generate-caption`),
never Groq or Gemini directly. Each function checks the user's login token
and a per-user hourly and daily limit (`consume_ai_quota`) before calling the
AI service. The API keys exist only as Supabase secrets. The trail generator
only sends real spots from the database to the model, and discards any stop
the model returns that doesn't match one of them.

---

## Project structure

```
wanderlens/
├── app/                      # Routes: one screen per file
│   ├── _layout.tsx           # Fonts, providers, the four auth guards
│   ├── (auth)/               # login, signup, forgot-password
│   ├── (tabs)/               # Feed, Map, Connect, Chat, Profile
│   ├── spot/[id].tsx         # Spot detail
│   ├── user/[id].tsx         # Public profile
│   ├── chat/                 # Conversation screen, archived chats
│   ├── group/[id].tsx        # Group info and management
│   ├── add-spot.tsx          # New spot (GPS / search / tap-to-pin)
│   ├── spot-camera.tsx       # Geo-tag camera
│   ├── pick-location.tsx     # Tap-to-pin map
│   ├── trail-generator.tsx   # AI photo trail
│   ├── my-trails.tsx         # Saved trails
│   ├── photo-studio.tsx      # Photo styles
│   ├── notes.tsx, note-editor.tsx
│   ├── notifications.tsx, saved.tsx, onboarding.tsx, edit-profile.tsx, ...
├── components/               # Shared UI (chat/ and skeletons/ subfolders)
├── context/                  # Auth, Chat, Notifications, Tour providers
├── hooks/                    # useUserLocation, useGoldenHour, ...
├── lib/                      # Supabase client, AI, geocoding, helpers
├── store/                    # Zustand stores for screen-to-screen handoff
├── constants/                # theme.ts (design tokens), countries, tour steps
├── supabase/
│   ├── migrations/           # Schema changes since tracking began
│   └── functions/            # Edge Functions: generate-trail,
│                             #   generate-caption, delete-account
├── app.json, app.config.js   # Expo config (static + config plugins)
└── eas.json                  # EAS build profiles
```

Every code file begins with a comment explaining its purpose, and each
function and major block has a short explanation, so the code can be read
file by file.

---

## Development

```bash
npm start            # dev server for the installed development app
npm run android      # build and install the development app (Android)
npm run ios          # same for iOS (macOS only)
npm run lint         # ESLint (expo lint)
npx tsc --noEmit     # type check; lint does not catch type errors
```

There are no automated tests yet. A change counts as done when lint and the

# NetShield-AI: Automated Network Intrusion Detection & Telemetry Analytics
> **23CSE301 Machine Learning Capstone Project**  
> Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity — CICIDS 2017 Dataset  
> **Author:** Aniruddha Mandal  
> **Institution:** Department of Computer Science & Engineering

[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11-blue?logo=python)](https://python.org)
[![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-1.x-orange?logo=scikit-learn)](https://scikit-learn.org)
[![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-2.x-green)](https://xgboost.readthedocs.io)
[![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.100+-teal?logo=fastapi)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com)
[![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/GUI-Streamlit-red?logo=streamlit)](https://streamlit.io)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow)](LICENSE)

---

## 1. Project Overview & Problem Statement

Modern enterprise defense infrastructure relies on automated machine learning pipelines to detect malicious cyber intrusions in line-rate network traffic. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) fail against polymorphic payloads, encrypted command-and-control channels, and zero-day exploits.

**NetShield-AI** implements an end-to-end Machine Learning pipeline across all three academic tracks prescribed by the **23CSE301 Capstone Guidelines**:
1. **Track 1: Regression (Review 1)** — Predicting continuous network telemetry latency (`log1p(Flow Duration)`) across 10 regression algorithms.
2. **Track 2: Classification (Review 1 Part A + Review 2 Part B)** — Binary discrimination between benign traffic and cyber intrusions across 10 distinct classification algorithms.
3. **Track 3: Clustering (Review 2)** — Unsupervised discovery of latent traffic patterns and attack sub-clusters using K-Means and Agglomerative Hierarchical clustering without ground-truth labels during training.
4. **Bonus Deliverable (+2 Marks)** — Interactive full-stack web application featuring a **FastAPI REST inference backend** and a **Streamlit live operations dashboard**.

---

## 2. Dataset Description: CICIDS 2017

The benchmark dataset was generated by the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (University of New Brunswick):
- **Traffic Volume:** 2,830,743 bidirectional flow records parsed across 8 CSV files.
- **Dimensionality:** 79 raw telemetry features extracted via CICFlowMeter, pruned and engineered down to 30 top predictors.
- **Attack Classes (15 categories):** BENIGN (80.3%), DoS Hulk, PortScan, DDoS, DoS GoldenEye, FTP-Patator, SSH-Patator, DoS Slowloris, DoS Slowhttptest, Botnets, Web Attacks (Brute Force, XSS, SQLi), Infiltration, and Heartbleed.
- **Zero Data Leakage Protocol:** All standard scalers and SMOTE balance generators are fitted strictly on training partitions; ground-truth labels are isolated from unsupervised clustering until post-hoc cross-tabulation.

---

## 3. Repository Architecture

```
NetShield-AI/
|-- 23CSE301_ML_26_27_Capstone_Guidelines.pdf  # Official academic curriculum guidelines
|-- IDS_ML_Project.ipynb                        # Master capstone notebook (all 3 tracks)
|-- notebooks/                                  # Fully executed track deep-dive notebooks
|   |-- regression.ipynb                        # 10 regression models, tuning & CV
|   |-- classification.ipynb                    # 10 classification models (Part A + B)
|   |-- clustering.ipynb                        # K-Means, Agglomerative, PCA & t-SNE
|-- src/                                        # Modular production-grade Python package
|   |-- data_loader.py                          # Phase 1: Ingestion & merging
|   |-- preprocessing.py                        # Phase 2: Missing, Inf & duplicate cleaning
|   |-- feature_engineering.py                  # Phase 3: Domain ratios & RF ranking
|   |-- data_split.py                           # Phase 4: Leakage-free split + SMOTE
|   |-- train_classification.py                 # Phase 5A: Review 1 Part A classifiers
|   |-- eval_classification.py                  # Phase 5B: Review 2 Part B & 10-model eval
|   |-- train_regression.py                     # Phase 6: 10 regression algorithms
|   |-- advanced_analytics.py                   # Phase 7: Cross-validation, PCA, Multiclass
|-- app/                                        # Interactive GUI Application (Bonus +2)
|   |-- backend.py                              # High-performance FastAPI REST API
|   |-- frontend.py                             # Interactive Streamlit operations dashboard
|   |-- app.py                                  # Dual-service unified process launcher
|-- models/                                     # Serialized inference models & metadata
|   |-- feature_metadata.json                   # Scaler means, variances & feature order
|   |-- sample_test_records.json                # Verified attack & benign verification vectors
|-- results/                                    # Generated diagnostic evaluation figures
|-- tests/
|   |-- test_app.py                             # Automated API verification test suite
|-- requirements.txt                            # Complete environment dependencies
`-- README.md                                   # Comprehensive documentation
```

---

## 4. Benchmark Results Across All Tracks

### 4.1 Track 1: Regression (Flow Duration Prediction)
Evaluated on the identical held-out test split using continuous target metric `log1p(Flow Duration)`:

| # | Algorithm | Category | R2 Score | RMSE | MAE | 5-Fold CV R2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B7** | **Random Forest Regressor** | Non-Linear Ensemble | **0.9999** | **0.0514** | **0.0211** | **0.9999 +/- 0.0001** |
| **B8** | **Gradient Boosting Regressor** | Stage-Wise Boosting | **0.9998** | **0.0682** | **0.0345** | **0.9998 +/- 0.0001** |
| **B6** | Decision Tree Regressor | Non-Parametric Tree | 0.9989 | 0.1294 | 0.0418 | - |
| **B10**| K-Nearest Neighbors Regressor | Metric Distance | 0.9954 | 0.2811 | 0.0892 | - |
| **B9** | Support Vector Regressor (SVR) | Dual Margin Kernel | 0.8845 | 1.4120 | 0.6510 | - |
| **B5** | Polynomial Regression (deg=2) | Non-Linear Basis | 0.7321 | 2.1890 | 1.4210 | - |
| **B1** | Linear Regression | Baseline Parametric | 0.6542 | 2.4831 | 1.7654 | - |
| **B2** | Ridge Regression | L2 Regularization | 0.6542 | 2.4831 | 1.7654 | - |
| **B4** | ElasticNet Regression | L1 + L2 Regularization | 0.6380 | 2.5401 | 1.8102 | - |
| **B3** | Lasso Regression | L1 Sparsity | 0.6210 | 2.5991 | 1.8650 | - |

*Hyperparameter Tuning: Randomized & Grid search on Random Forest and Ridge; 5-fold CV confirms generalization within +/- 0.01%.*

---

### 4.2 Track 2: Classification (Consolidated 10-Algorithm Benchmark)
Evaluated on the identical held-out test partition with ground-truth binary labels:

| Rank | Algorithm | Curriculum Scope | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | Weighted F1 | ROC-AUC |
|:---:|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **1** | **Random Forest Classifier** | **Review 2 (Part B)** | **0.9958** | **0.9804** | **0.9953** | **0.9878** | **0.9999** |
| **2** | **Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)** | **Review 2 (Part B)** | **0.9951** | **0.9742** | **0.9974** | **0.9857** | **0.9999** |
| **3** | **Decision Tree Classifier** | **Review 1 (Part A)** | 0.9946 | 0.9746 | 0.9941 | 0.9843 | 0.9990 |
| **4** | **Bagging Classifier (DT Base)** | **Review 2 (Part B)** | 0.9945 | 0.9737 | 0.9945 | 0.9840 | 0.9995 |
| **5** | **K-Nearest Neighbors (k=7)** | **Review 1 (Part A)** | 0.9831 | 0.9481 | 0.9520 | 0.9501 | 0.9959 |
| **6** | **MLP Neural Network** | **Review 2 (Part B)** | 0.9774 | 0.8915 | 0.9864 | 0.9365 | 0.9971 |
| **7** | **Support Vector Classifier (SVC)**| **Review 1 (Part A)** | 0.9599 | 0.8402 | 0.9414 | 0.8879 | 0.9854 |
| **8** | **AdaBoost Classifier** | **Review 2 (Part B)** | 0.9476 | 0.7937 | 0.9315 | 0.8571 | 0.9726 |
| **9** | **Logistic Regression** | **Review 1 (Part A)** | 0.9079 | 0.6587 | 0.9431 | 0.7757 | 0.9726 |
| **10**| **Gaussian Naive Bayes** | **Review 1 (Part A)** | 0.2566 | 0.1840 | 0.9907 | 0.3103 | 0.6403 |

**Champion Model Selection:** **Random Forest Classifier** is selected as the production champion based on:
- Top-ranked Weighted F1-Score (0.9878) and ROC-AUC (0.9999).
- Near-zero false-negative rate on stealthy scans and brute force exploits.
- Ultra-low inference latency (< 0.05 ms per flow), allowing line-rate filtering without GPU acceleration.

---

### 4.3 Track 3: Clustering (Unsupervised Anomaly Discovery)
Trained with zero label guidance on standardized feature space:

| Algorithm | Chosen Cluster Count (k) | Silhouette Score | Davies-Bouldin Index | Calinski-Harabasz Index | Diagnostic Plot |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| **K-Means Clustering** | **k = 3** | **0.9946** | **0.1305** | **205,079.63** | Elbow Curve (inflection at k=3) |
| **Agglomerative Hierarchical** | **k = 3** (Ward Linkage) | **0.9946** | **0.1305** | **205,079.63** | Dendrogram (3 primary branches) |

- **PCA 2D Projection:** Principal components PC1 and PC2 cleanly segregate volumetric attack flows from standard HTTP/HTTPS communications.
- **t-SNE Manifold:** Confirms compact, dense clusters corresponding to repetitive automated scanning patterns.
- **Post-Hoc Cross-Tabulation:** Confirms Cluster 0 captures 99.8% of normal operational traffic, while Clusters 1 & 2 isolate high-frequency flooding anomalies.

---

## 5. Bonus Deliverable: Interactive Web Application (+2 Marks)

The project includes a production-grade interactive GUI designed with modern software engineering principles:
- **Backend (FastAPI):** High-speed asynchronous REST API providing validation, input scaling, and sub-millisecond model predictions.
- **Frontend (Streamlit):** Security Operations Center (SOC) dashboard allowing live payload testing, model switching, threshold adjustment, and risk analysis.

### Launching the Application

1. **Option A — Unified Single-Command Launcher:**
```bash
python app/app.py
```

2. **Option B — Launch Backend and Frontend Separately:**
```bash
# Terminal 1: Start FastAPI REST Backend (Port 8000)
uvicorn app.backend:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload

# Terminal 2: Start Streamlit Frontend (Port 8501)
streamlit run app/frontend.py
```

Access the dashboard at **http://localhost:8501** (API documentation available at **http://localhost:8000/docs**).

### Automated App Testing
Run the test suite to verify end-to-end functionality:
```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_app.py -v
```
All endpoints and real attack classifications pass with 100% accuracy.

---

## 6. How to Run the Pipeline

### Step 1: Environment Setup
```bash
git clone https://github.com/ANDROIDREV-9/NetShield-AI.git
cd NetShield-AI
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Step 2: Run Individual Pipeline Modules

### Step 3: View Notebooks
Each track is fully executed with all outputs and figures visible:

# CareerPilot AI — An AI Career Assistant

> Built with Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Gemini 3.8 Flash for the Google Cloud *Build with Gemini* workshop.

---

## 🌟 Executive Summary & Motivation

In today's fast-evolving technology landscape, job seekers and career pivoters frequently face challenges:
- Assessing whether their background genuinely matches modern job descriptions.
- Translating missing skills into concrete, actionable study plans.
- Receiving objective, rubric-driven feedback on practice interview questions.

**CareerPilot AI** is an intelligent, agent-first copilot that bridges these gaps. It provides deterministic resume parsing, automated job-fit gap analysis, structured learning roadmaps with capstone project recommendations, role-specific interview coaching using the STAR framework, cross-turn candidate preference memory, A2UI visual cards, and Firestore cloud persistence.

---

## 📸 Website & Application Previews

### 1. Modern Glassmorphic Web Application (`http://localhost:8081`)
Features one-click quick actions for candidate memory, resume gap analytics, customized roadmaps, and STAR interview evaluations.

![CareerPilot AI Dashboard](docs/images/careerpilot_dashboard.png)

### 2. Live AI Answers & Candidate Memory in Action
Demonstrates multi-turn memory recall, target profile retrieval, and structured career recommendations generated by the agent.

![CareerPilot AI Conversation & Answers](docs/images/careerpilot_ai_conversation.png)

### 3. Google ADK Developer Playground (`http://localhost:8080`)
Interactive developer environment rendering agent reasoning, A2UI card layouts, tool calls, and Vertex AI Memory Bank durable fact extraction.

![Google ADK Developer Playground](docs/images/adk_playground.png)

---

## 🏗️ Architecture & How It Works

```
                     +----------------------------------------+
                     |         User / Candidate Input        |
                     +----------------------------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
                     +----------------------------------------+
                     |         Google ADK Agent Engine        |
                     |       (Gemini 3.8 Flash Model)         |
                     +----------------------------------------+
                                         |
        +-------------------+------------+------------+--------------------+
        |                   |                         |                    |
        v                   v                         v                    v
+----------------+  +----------------+        +----------------+  +------------------+
| Profile Memory |  | Resume Parsing |        | Gap & Roadmap  |  | Mock Interview   |
|   & Goals      |  | & Extraction   |        |   Engine       |  | Coaching & STAR  |
+----------------+  +----------------+        +----------------+  +------------------+
        |                   |                         |                    |
        +-------------------+------------+------------+--------------------+
                                         |
                                         v
                     +----------------------------------------+
                     |      Calibrated Output & Coaching      |
                     |      (CLI or ADK Web Playground)       |
                     +----------------------------------------+
```

### 1. The Reasoning Model (`gemini-3.8-flash`)
Acts as the central orchestrator and dialogue partner. It understands nuanced intent, interprets conversational career queries, synthesizes unstructured insights, and decides when to execute specific tools.

### 2. Core Deterministic Tools (`career_pilot/tools.py`)
To prevent hallucinations and guarantee consistent results, the agent utilizes deterministic function tools:
- **`get_candidate_profile`**: Recalls the candidate's active target role, target seniority, verified skills, identified gaps, and mock interview practice history across turns.
- **`update_candidate_profile`**: Updates career aspirations, target seniority levels, or records newly acquired skills.
- **`list_sample_profiles`**: Discovers pre-loaded resumes and target job profiles for testing.
- **`load_sample_resume` / `load_sample_job_description`**: Retrieves benchmark profiles offline without external API dependencies.
- **`parse_resume_content`**: Extracts technical skills, years of experience, and section structure.
- **`compare_resume_with_job`**: Performs gap analysis, skill matching, unverified credential detection, and career pivot detection.
- **`generate_learning_roadmap`**: Generates a 6-to-8 week milestone learning plan complete with capstone project recommendations.
- **`evaluate_interview_response`**: Evaluates practice answers against a quantitative rubric (Clarity, Technical Depth, STAR framework) and suggests concrete improvements.

---

## 🧪 Evaluation & Robustness

The codebase includes an automated test suite verifying edge cases:
- **Normal Resumes:** Successfully extracts multi-tier skills and experience estimates.
- **Incomplete / Malformed Inputs:** Gracefully handles resumes with missing sections or limited data without failing.
- **Unrelated Careers / Pivot Detection:** Detects when a candidate's background is completely mismatched (e.g., software engineering vs. nursing) and flags career-pivot requirements.
- **Interview Rubric Calibration:** Penalizes overly brief answers (e.g. "I restarted the server") and rewards structured, metrics-driven responses.

All automated tests run via Python's standard `unittest` framework:
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
```

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- Google Cloud Project with Vertex AI enabled
- Google ADK (`pip install google-adk`)

### 1. Environment Setup
Configure your environment variables in `career_pilot/.env`:
```bash
GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true
GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-gcp-project-id
GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global
```

### 2. Run the Automated Tests
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
```

### 3. Interactive CLI Testing
```bash
# Discover sample profiles
adk run career_pilot "List the available sample test profiles so I can test you."

# Check candidate memory
adk run career_pilot "What do you remember about my current career profile and target role?"

# Run gap analysis and generate a learning roadmap
adk run career_pilot "Compare the junior_software_engineer resume with the ai_ml_engineer job description, show matched and missing skills, and give me a learning roadmap."

# Practice mock interview coaching
adk run career_pilot "Ask me a technical interview question for an AI/ML Engineer role, and evaluate my answer: 'When building a RAG application, I chunk documents with overlap, generate embeddings using text-embedding-004, and evaluate retrieval precision.'"
```

### 4. Interactive Web Playground
Launch the ADK web interface:
```bash
adk web --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 .
```
Navigate to `http://localhost:8000` in your browser and select `career_pilot`.

---

## 🛡️ Ethical Guardrails & Truthfulness

- **No False Live Job Claims:** The agent explicitly clarifies that it evaluates provided and benchmark profiles rather than claiming live access to external job boards.
- **Fair & Constructive Coaching:** Rubric evaluations emphasize growth, highlighting both current strengths and actionable next steps.
- **Privacy & Security:** Environment credentials and API tokens are excluded via `.gitignore`.

# Helios Terminal **AI-Powered Multi-Agent Decision Intelligence Platform** *AI sourcing strategy and dependency risk analysis* [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Python 3.11](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3110/) [![React 18](https://img.shields.io/badge/react-18.0-cyan.svg)](https://react.dev/) [![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/fastapi-0.104-green.svg)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)
--- ## 🎯 Overview Helios Terminal is a sophisticated decision intelligence platform that analyzes AI sourcing decisions (build/buy/outsource) and their long-term dependency risks. It takes a concrete decision brief and returns a comparative analysis of each path's hidden costs and lock-in risks. **🔍 One Decision at a Time** — Focuses on single sourcing decisions with deep analysis rather than broad, shallow recommendations. **🔗 Dependency Risk Mapping** — Identifies lock-in mechanisms, failure modes, and long-term consequences of each sourcing option. **✅ Verification-Gated Pipeline** — Six-agent pipeline with cross-stage verification ensuring claims are grounded in sources before propagation. --- ## 🚀 Problem Statement Every organization adopting AI faces the same critical decision: build capability in-house, license a model, or outsource to vendors. Each path creates different dependency structures that may only surface years later through: - Vendor term changes and pricing shifts - License expirations and compliance risks - Partner acquisition or discontinuation - Technical debt and migration costs Today these decisions are made on instinct and vendor pitches without structured visibility into long-term dependency risks. --- ## 💡 Solution Helios answers one fundamental question: **Which sourcing option creates the least dangerous long-term dependency?** **Input:** Entity, capability needed, candidate options (or auto-inferred) **Process:** Six-agent analysis pipeline with verification gates **Output:** Comparative verdict with lock-in analysis, severity scoring, and dependency graph ### Pipeline Architecture ``` Decision Brief │ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ │ Ingestion │ ← Context gathering (web search + structured sources) └──────┬───────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ │Stack-Mapping │ ← AI-stack layer identification └──────┬───────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ │Scenario-Generation│ ← Realistic path enumeration └──────┬───────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────┐ │Outcome-Prediction│ ← Future trajectory projection └──────┬───────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────┐ │Dependency-Diagnosis │ ← Lock-in identification & failure modes └──────┬──────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ │ Orchestrator │ ← Comparative verdict synthesis └──────┬───────┘ │ ▼ Comparative Verdict ``` ### Agent Capabilities | Agent | Function | |-------|----------| | **Ingestion** | Gathers decision-specific context via web search + structured sources (HF Hub, BIS Entity List) | | **Stack-Mapping** | Identifies relevant AI-stack layers for the decision | | **Scenario-Generation** | Enumerates realistic sourcing paths (build/buy/outsource variants) | | **Outcome-Prediction** | Projects plausible future trajectories for each path | | **Dependency-Diagnosis** | Identifies lock-in mechanisms and failure modes per outcome | | **Orchestrator** | Synthesizes comparative verdict with severity scoring | Each top-level agent orchestrates 2–3 sub-agents (18 LLM-calling components total). Between stages, a **cross-stage verification layer** validates claims against cited sources, registering each as `grounded_in` sources or `inference`. --- ## 🛠️ Tech Stack ### Frontend - **Framework:** React 18 + Vite - **Language:** TypeScript - **Styling:** Tailwind CSS with custom design tokens - **State Management:** TanStack Query - **Routing:** React Router - **Visualization:** react-flow (`@xyflow/react`) ### Backend - **Framework:** FastAPI (Python 3.11) - **Validation:** Pydantic v2 - **Testing:** pytest (350+ tests, fully mocked) ### Multi-Agent Pipeline - **Architecture:** Hand-rolled stage-gated orchestration - **Pattern:** Sequential agents with parallel sub-agents - **Design:** No external agent framework dependency ### LLM Integration - **Client:** Provider-agnostic wrapper (`backend/app/llm/client.py`) - **Default:** DeepSeek V4 Flash - **Alternatives:** OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI (switchable via env vars) ### Grounding & Retrieval - **Web Search:** Tavily API for context augmentation - **Verification:** Cross-stage claim validation against sources --- ## 📁 Project Structure ``` helios-terminal/ ├── backend/ # FastAPI API + multi-agent pipeline │ ├── app/ │ │ ├── agents/ # Six parent agents + 18 sub-agents │ │ ├── api/ # REST endpoints + schemas │ │ ├── llm/ # LLM client wrapper │ │ ├── pipeline/ # Stage-gated orchestration │ │ ├── retrieval/ # Web search retrieval │ │ └── verification/ # Claim validation layer │ └── tests/ # 350+ pytest tests ├── frontend/ # React terminal UI │ ├── src/ │ │ ├── components/ # Decision input, status, verdict, graph │ │ ├── pages/ # Route components │ │ └── lib/ # API client + utilities ├── docs/ # Product & architecture documentation │ ├── frontend-docs/ # Interface-specific docs │ └── *.md # PRD, vision, architecture, TASKS ├── infra/ # Docker & deployment configs └── .github/ # CI workflows ``` --- ## 🚦 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python 3.11+** - **Node.js 18+** - **API Keys:** LLM provider + [Tavily](https://app.tavily.com) ### Backend Setup ```bash cd backend pip install -r requirements.txt cp .env.example .env # Configure your API keys uvicorn app.main:app --reload ``` **Environment Variables** (`.env`): ```env LLM_PROVIDER=deepseek # or openrouter DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=your_key # or OPENROUTER_API_KEY TAVILY_API_KEY=your_key ``` **Run Tests:** ```bash cd backend python -m pytest # 350+ tests, fully mocked ``` ### Frontend Setup ```bash cd frontend npm install npm run dev ``` Open `http://localhost:5173` — expects backend at `http://localhost:8000` **Custom Backend URL:** ```env # frontend/.env.local VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ``` --- ## 📊 Usage ### Web Interface 1. Enter entity and capability 2. Add candidate options (optional — Helios can infer) 3. Submit and watch the six-stage pipeline progress 4. Review comparative verdict with path cards and dependency graph ### API Usage ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "entity": "Indian Army signals division", "capability": "small language model for edge inference", "options": ["build in-house", "license open-weight"] }' ``` **Response includes:** - `verdict.recommended_path` — Optimal sourcing choice - `verdict.verdict_summary` — High-level analysis - `verdict.cross_path_comparison.path_comparisons[]` — Per-path analysis with severity scores - `verification_passed` / `verification_failed_stage` — Audit trail See [docs/frontend-docs/07_API_CONTRACT.md](docs/frontend-docs/07_API_CONTRACT.md) for full API specification. --- ## ✨ Current Status ### ✅ Completed (Phases 1–10 & Phase 12) - **Six-Agent Verified Pipeline:** Full multi-agent reasoning with cross-stage verification and bounded recalibration loops. - **Multi-Provider LLM Resilience:** Automated fallback chain across NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, and DeepSeek Direct with cooldown tracking. - **Institutional Bloomberg Workstation (`/dashboard`):** 9 F-key dedicated workstation views, `` command bar, and Web Audio API procedural sound engine. - **Executive User Dashboard (`/user-dashboard`):** Modern 7-view executive console with real-time Posture Scoring, Tech Sovereignty Index, Supply Chain Chokepoint mapping, and printable audit dossiers. - **Universal Dual-Theme Engine:** Obsidian Dark Mode and Alabaster Light Mode with zero-flicker CSS tokens and `localStorage` persistence. - **Sticky Frosted Glass Navigation:** Viewport-pinned headers with dynamic scroll blur, elevation, and CSS clipping fix. - **Interactive Cinema Demo Player (`/demo`):** Browser-native bilingual (English & Hinglish) Web Speech Synthesis narration engine with synchronized 7-scene presentation and live subtitles. - **Complete Test Coverage:** 350+ passing pytest tests and strict TypeScript type-checking. ### 📋 Next Steps (Phase 11) - Docker containerization & docker-compose production orchestration - Cloud deployment configurations (Vercel + Render) - CI/CD automation pipelines --- ### 📚 Documentation - **[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)** — Complete 3-tier system architecture, multi-agent pipeline, and multi-provider fallback chain - **[docs/FEATURES.md](docs/FEATURES.md)** — Comprehensive feature matrix (Pipeline, Executive Dashboard, Bloomberg Terminal, Themes, Audio) - **[docs/TECH_STACK.md](docs/TECH_STACK.md)** — Technology choices and detailed library rationale - **[docs/USER_DASHBOARD_AND_THEMING.md](docs/USER_DASHBOARD_AND_THEMING.md)** — Executive User Dashboard (`/user-dashboard`), dual-theming engine, and bilingual demo player specification - **[docs/PRD.md](docs/PRD.md)** — Product requirements document & functional specs (FR-1 to FR-14) - # CYRV capstone project

Analysis of the CYRV e-commerce dataset (Brazilian online marketplace orders).
See [`data/README.md`](data/README.md) for what each data file contains.

## Repo structure

- `data/` — the dataset used for analysis. See its README for details. GitHub blocks files over 100MB, so be careful not to add more/larger data files here — the geolocation file is already close to that.
- `src/cyrv/` — shared code, packaged as `cyrv` so it can be imported anywhere with `import cyrv`. Optional — you can also just write standalone scripts here and run them directly, no import needed.
- `notebooks/` — Jupyter notebooks for exploration and analysis.
- `pyproject.toml` — project dependencies, managed with `uv`.

## Setup with uv

[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) manages the Python version, virtual
environment, and dependencies for this project. Install it first if you don't
have it (see the uv docs), then from the project root:

```bash
uv sync
```

This creates a `.venv/` folder and installs everything listed in
`pyproject.toml`. Run any script or notebook kernel through `uv`, so it uses
that environment:

```bash
uv run src/my_script.py
uv run jupyter lab
```

## Managing dependencies

Add a new package:

```bash
uv add pandas
```

Remove one:

```bash
uv remove pandas
```

This updates `pyproject.toml` and the lock file (`uv.lock`) automatically —
don't edit dependencies by hand. Commit both files so everyone uses the same
versions.

# 🚀 Employee Leave Management System – DevOps CI/CD Pipeline

A complete end-to-end DevOps capstone project demonstrating modern software delivery: **Code → Automated Testing → SonarQube Quality Analysis → Docker Containerization → Jenkins CI/CD → Continuous Deployment → Prometheus & Grafana Observability**.

---

## 🌟 Key Features

1. **Employee Portal**:
   - Authenticated leave submission with real-time day calculation.
   - Live leave balance tracking across multiple leave categories.
   - Application status lifecycle (`PENDING` ⏳ → `APPROVED` ✅ / `REJECTED` ❌).
   - Ability to cancel pending requests.

2. **HR / Manager Portal**:
   - Real-time review queue of submitted leave applications across departments.
   - 1-click Approval or Rejection with custom manager remarks.
   - Status filtering and audit tracking.

3. **Admin Portal**:
   - Employee directory management (Create, Update, Delete).
   - Leave quota configuration (Casual, Sick, Paid, Maternity/Paternity).
   - Company-wide leave history and analytics.

4. **DevOps Live Telemetry Hub**:
   - Live application telemetry (`/health`, `/metrics`).
   - Interactive 1-click role switcher for smooth lab demonstrations.
   - Built-in Prometheus scraper metrics (`prom-client`).

---

## 🏗️ DevOps Architecture

```text
[Developer Workstation]
         │ (git commit & push)
         ▼
  [Git Repository] ──(Webhook Trigger)──┐
                                        ▼
                                 [Jenkins CI/CD]
                                        │
           ┌────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐
           ▼                            ▼                            ▼
   [Stage 1: Checkout]          [Stage 2: Build]          [Stage 3: Jest Tests]
                                                                     │ (Fail? Stop ❌)
                                                                     ▼ (Pass? ✅)
   [Stage 6: Deployment]       [Stage 5: Docker]        [Stage 4: SonarQube]
           │                    (Container Build)        (Static Code Analysis)
           ▼
[Docker Container :8080] ◄──────────────┘
         │
         ├─── Scraped by ───► [Prometheus :9090] ───► [Grafana Dashboards :3000]
         └─── Connected to ──► [MySQL / SQLite Database]
```

---

## 🛠️ Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | HTML5, Vanilla CSS3 (Glassmorphism), Vanilla JavaScript | Responsive, rich dark-mode UI |
| **Backend API** | Node.js (v20+) + Express.js | REST API & routing |
| **Database** | SQLite (built-in zero-config) & MySQL 8.0 | Relational data persistence |
| **Testing** | Jest + Supertest | Automated unit & integration tests |
| **Containerization**| Docker & Docker Compose | Lightweight portable containers |
| **CI/CD** | Jenkins Declarative Pipeline (`Jenkinsfile`) | Automated pipeline orchestration |
| **Code Quality** | SonarQube Scanner (`sonar-project.properties`) | Static code analysis & test coverage |
| **Monitoring** | Prometheus (`prom-client`) + Grafana | Telemetry & business metrics |

---

## 🚀 Quick Start Guide

### 1. Run Standalone (Local Development)

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies
npm install

# 2. Run automated test suite (17/17 tests)
npm test

# 3. Start application
npm start
```

Open your browser at **[http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080)**.

### 2. Run with Docker

```bash
# Build Docker image
docker build -t employee-leave-management .

# Run container
docker run -d --name employee-leave-app -p 8080:8080 employee-leave-management
```

### 3. Run Full DevOps Stack (App + MySQL + Prometheus + Grafana)

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

- **Web Application**: `http://localhost:8080`
- **Prometheus UI**: `http://localhost:9090`
- **Grafana Dashboard**: `http://localhost:3000` (User: `admin`, Pass: `admin`)
- **Health Check Probe**: `http://localhost:8080/health`
- **Prometheus Metrics Endpoint**: `http://localhost:8080/metrics`

---

## 👥 Demo Credentials (1-Click Switcher Available in UI)

| Role | Name | Email | Password |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Employee** | John Doe | `john.doe@company.com` | `password123` |
| **HR / Manager** | Sarah Connor | `manager@company.com` | `manager123` |
| **DevOps Admin** | System Admin | `admin@company.com` | `admin123` |

---

## 📋 College Lab Demonstration Script

### Part 1: Application Demonstration

1. Open `http://localhost:8080`.
2. Notice the **Live Lab Demo Hub** ribbon at the top.
3. Click **👤 John Doe (Employee)**:
   - Show the leave quota cards (Casual, Sick, Earned).
   - Click **Apply For Leave**, pick dates and enter reason, then click **Submit**.
   - Show that the new request appears in the table with status `PENDING` ⏳.
4. Click **👩‍💼 Sarah (HR Manager)**:
   - Notice the approval request counter.
   - Click **Approve** on John's request, provide remarks ("Approved!"), and confirm.
   - Status transitions to `APPROVED` ✅.
5. Click **👤 John Doe (Employee)** again:
   - John now sees his leave as `APPROVED` with the updated quota balance.
6. Click **🛠️ DevOps Admin**:
   - Demonstrate adding a new employee or managing leave types.

### Part 2: DevOps CI/CD Demonstration

1. Show `Jenkinsfile` in repository:
   - Explain the 7 automated stages: `Checkout` → `Install` → `Test` → `SonarQube` → `Docker Build` → `Deploy` → `Verification`.
2. Demonstrate automated tests:
   ```bash
   npm test
   ```
   Show how tests validate authentication, role restrictions, and date logic before build proceeds.
3. Demonstrate Docker containerization:
   - Show `Dockerfile` (multi-stage Alpine image, non-root user, healthcheck).
   - Run `docker ps` to show the running container.
4. Show Healthcheck & Prometheus Metrics:
   - Navigate to `http://localhost:8080/health` (Shows JSON with UP status and DB dialect).
   - Navigate to `http://localhost:8080/metrics` (Shows Prometheus counters for HTTP requests and leave lifecycle metrics).

---

## 🎯 Viva Examination Q&A Guide

**Q1: What is the benefit of containerizing this application with Docker?**  
> *Answer:* Docker packages the application along with its Node.js runtime and dependencies into a lightweight image. This eliminates the "it works on my machine" problem and guarantees identical execution in development, Jenkins CI, and production.

**Q2: What happens if an automated test fails during the Jenkins pipeline?**  
> *Answer:* The pipeline automatically terminates at Stage 3 (`Run Automated Tests`). The broken build is never containerized or deployed to production, ensuring continuous quality and reliability.

**Q3: How does the monitoring integration work?**  
> *Answer:* The Node.js application exposes a `/metrics` endpoint using `prom-client`. Prometheus periodically scrapes this endpoint every 5 seconds to collect latency, memory, and custom leave counters, which Grafana visualizes.

# Weather & Budget-Smart Bangladesh Tourist Planner

SE331 Software Engineering Design Capstone Project - Fall 2026
Department of Software Engineering, Daffodil International University
Group 05 · Lab Section 42 D1
A full-stack web application that helps tourists plan trips across Bangladesh by combining live weather
data with realistic budget estimation: destination browsing, itinerary builder, weather suitability
scores and alerts, best-time recommendations, budget estimator, expense tracker, budget-based destination
recommendations and an admin panel.

## Tech stack

| Layer        | Technology                                            |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend     | React.js (Vite), React Router, Recharts, Tailwind CSS |
| Backend      | Node.js, Express.js (REST API, JWT authentication)    |
| Database     | MySQL (XAMPP)                                         |
| Weather data | Open-Meteo API (free, no key)                         |

## Team

| Member   | Name           | ID         |
| -------- | -------------- | ---------- |
| Member 1 | Efaz Al Tasin  | 241-35-526 |
| Member 2 | Rubaiyat Ratul | 241-35-344 |
| Member 3 | Md. Raj Aryan  | 241-35-545 |

## Getting started

Requirements: Node.js 20+, Git, XAMPP (MySQL).

1. Start **MySQL** in the XAMPP Control Panel.
2. Backend

```bash
cd server
npm install
cp .env.example .env # Windows: copy .env.example .env (then edit JWT_SECRET)
npm run db:setup # creates the database, tables and sample data
npm run dev # http://localhost:5000
```

3. Frontend (new terminal)

```bash
cd client
npm install
npm run dev # http://localhost:5173
```

Demo accounts: `admin@tourist.com / Admin@123` and `tourist@example.com / Tourist@123`.

## Project structure

```
server/ Express API (src/routes, src/middleware, src/utils, sql, scripts)
client/ React app (src/pages, src/components, src/context, src/lib)
```

Pages in `client/src/pages` and routers in `server/src/routes` are auto-registered, and
`components/*-widgets` folders are plug-in areas, so each member can add features without editing shared
files.

## Non-functional requirements

Performance (gzip, caching, indexes, pagination), security (bcrypt, JWT, RBAC, validation, sanitisation,
parameterised SQL, helmet, rate limiting) and responsive, accessible UI (Tailwind, Chrome/Firefox/Edge).

## Git workflow

Feature branches (`feature/<name>`), conventional commit messages, pull requests reviewed by a teammate,
merged with a merge commit (no squash) so every commit stays visible.

# EECS4480 – Capstone Project  
## Title: Developing a Neural Network Model to Detect Phishing Emails with Gmail API Integration

This repository contains my EECS4480 capstone project: a BERT-based phishing email detection system that:

- Trains on multiple real-world phishing and ham email datasets  
- Evaluates robustness using adversarial text attacks (TextFooler, BAE)  
- Integrates with the **Gmail API** to classify emails directly from a live inbox  

The project is implemented in **Jupyter Notebooks** using **PyTorch**, **HuggingFace Transformers**, **TextAttack**, and the **Gmail API**.

---

## Repository Structure
```
EECS4480---Capstone-Project/
├── notebooks/
│   ├── 01_preprocess.ipynb                # Data loading & preprocessing
│   ├── 02_train_bert.ipynb                # BERT training & fine-tuning
│   ├── 03_train_with_TextAttack.ipynb     # Adversarial robustness training
│   ├── 04_analysis.ipynb                  # Evaluation, metrics, confusion matrices
│   ├── 05_eval_synthetic.ipynb            # Synthetic dataset evaluation
│   ├── 06_Gmail_integration.ipynb         # Gmail API integration & inbox predictions
│   └── ...
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

---

## Features

- **BERT-based classifier** for phishing vs ham  
- Supports multiple real-world datasets  
- Evaluation metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score

- **Gmail API integration** for live inbox predictions

# Herbal-Ai — Philippine Medicinal Plants Repository

Herbal-Ai is a full-stack educational repository for documenting and sharing Philippine medicinal-plant knowledge. It combines a curated plant library, source-grounded AI assistance, community features, and an administrative review workflow. It is not a diagnostic service, a prescribing system, or an institutional DOH/PITAHC product.

---

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client[Next.js 16 Web Client]
    API[Express 5 / Node.js API Gateway]
    Socket[Socket.io Real-Time Engine]
    DB[(PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector)]
    Gemini[Google Gemini API]
    Cloudinary[Cloudinary Media Storage]

    Client -->|REST API / HTTPS| API
    Client <-->|WebSocket / WSS| Socket
    API -->|Prisma ORM / SQL| DB
    API -->|Embeddings & Chat Synthesis| Gemini
    API -->|Image Uploads| Cloudinary
```

---

## Core Features

1. **Philippine Medicinal Plants Catalog**
   * Includes the 10 medicinal plants commonly identified in Philippine DOH reference materials (*Lagundi, Sambong, Ampalaya, Bawang, Bayabas, Yerba Buena, Tsaang Gubat, Akapulko, Niyog-niyogan, Ulasimang Bato*) alongside additional reviewed Philippine plant records.
   * Local, scientific, and regional (Cebuano/Tagalog) names, preparation steps, dosages, and contraindications.
   * Semantic vector search via 768-dimension embeddings (`pgvector`).

2. **Dr. Ai — Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Assistant**
   * Educational assistant that organizes relevant repository records into clear answers with source references and safety boundaries.
   * Refuses unsupported herb-specific guidance when the repository lacks a sufficiently relevant verified source.
   * Session-based memory, input boundary protection, and rate limiting (30 requests / 10 minutes).

3. **Contributor Suggestions & Administrative Moderation**
   * Community submission workflow with administrative review panel.
   * Multi-channel notifications (in-app dropdown, real-time WebSocket push, and email).
   * Immutable Administrative Audit Logging (`APPROVE`, `REJECT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `BAN`, `UNBAN`).

4. **Community Forums & Real-Time Direct Messaging**
   * Category-based threaded discussions with nested comments.
   * Secure, JWT-authenticated 1-on-1 private messaging with image attachments.

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technologies |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Frontend** | Next.js 16 (React 19), TypeScript, Vanilla CSS, Lucide Icons, Socket.io-Client, Recharts |
| **Backend** | Node.js 22, Express 5, TypeScript, Prisma ORM, Socket.io, Nodemailer, Bcrypt, Zod |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL 16 with `pgvector` extension |
| **AI / NLP** | Google Gemini API (`gemini-embedding-2`; configurable Flash models, default `gemini-3.6-flash`) |
| **Testing** | Vitest, Supertest |
| **DevOps & CI/CD** | Docker, Docker Compose, GitHub Actions |

---

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites
* Node.js v20+ or v22+
* npm v10+
* PostgreSQL 16 (with `pgvector` extension enabled) or a cloud instance (e.g. Neon)
* Google Gemini API Key

---

### Local Installation & Setup

#### 1. Clone the Repository
```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-username/herbal-ai.git
cd herbal-ai
```

#### 2. Backend Setup
```bash
cd herbalaibackend
npm install
```

Configure `herbalaibackend/.env`:
```env
PORT=5000
NODE_ENV=development
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/herbalai?sslmode=disable"
JWT_SECRET="your-super-secret-jwt-key"
JWT_REFRESH_SECRET="your-super-secret-refresh-key"
FRONTEND_URL="http://localhost:3000"
GEMINI_API_KEY="your-gemini-api-key"
DR_AI_CHAT_MODELS="gemini-3.6-flash,gemini-3.1-flash-lite,gemini-3.8-flash,gemini-3.7-flash"
DR_AI_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS=7000
DR_AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096
DR_AI_MAX_MODEL_ATTEMPTS=4
DR_AI_MODEL_COOLDOWN_MS=60000
```

`DR_AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` defaults to 4096 and is clamped to 2048–8192. Thinking models use generation headroom for both reasoning and visible answers, so a short visible reply can still reach the output limit. The larger default does not relax source-grounding, safety, completion validation, credit refunds or request deadlines. Generation logs record only bounded token counts and normalized terminal reasons, not prompts, answers, thoughts or credentials. Increase allowance only after checking provider usage and latency; a successful model response does not establish medical accuracy.

Chat controller failure responses use the shared `AiRequestError` contract for JSON and terminal SSE errors: a safe `message`, `code`, `retryable`, and `creditStatus`. Existing `AI_RESPONSE_INCOMPLETE` and `AI_RESPONSE_BLOCKED` codes are retained; generic provider/deadline failures use `AI_UNAVAILABLE`, and credit validation/settlement errors use `AI_CREDIT_ERROR`. Pre-controller authentication, rate-limit and schema-validation responses retain their existing contracts.

Do not promise a refund when `creditStatus` is `recovery_pending`: preserve the draft and reconcile the wallet before another paid attempt. Recovery-pending, safety-blocked and credit errors have `retryable: false`; other generation errors permit a user-confirmed retry only after reconciling any ambiguous result. This flag is not an instruction to retry automatically. Replayed completed answers use the original idempotency key without another debit. These controller diagnostics log normalized error codes rather than raw provider messages; other provider-layer diagnostics remain separate.

Initialize the database and load the configured seed catalog:
```bash
npx prisma generate
npx prisma db push
npm run seed
```

Start backend development server:
```bash
npm run dev
```

#### 3. Frontend Setup
```bash
cd ../herbalaifrontend
npm install
```

Configure `herbalaifrontend/.env.local`:
```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="http://localhost:5000/api"
NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL="http://localhost:5000"
```

Start frontend development server:
```bash
npm run dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser.

#### Production-mode capstone demonstration (Windows)

For a faster, stable demonstration without development overlays or on-demand compilation:

```powershell
.\scripts\start-demo.ps1
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. When the demonstration is finished:

```powershell
.\scripts\stop-demo.ps1
```

The start script performs clean backend and frontend production builds, launches both services in production mode, and verifies their health before reporting readiness. Runtime logs are written to the ignored `.demo-logs` directory. Demo email defaults to safe `log` mode; explicitly set `EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=allowlist` and `EMAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS` before starting only when a controlled mailbox test is required.

---

### Running with Docker Compose (One-Click Setup)

To run the complete system (PostgreSQL with `pgvector`, Express API backend, and Next.js frontend):

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Services will be available at:
* **Frontend Web Client**: `http://localhost:3000`
* **Backend API Gateway**: `http://localhost:5000/api`
* **PostgreSQL Database**: `localhost:5432`

### Production VPS Deployment (Hostinger / DigitalOcean / AWS)

For deploying to an Ubuntu VPS with Nginx reverse proxy, automatic SSL (Certbot), and zero-downtime updates, follow the complete guide in **[Docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md](Docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md)**:

```bash
# 1. Setup Docker on VPS
./scripts/setup-docker.sh

# 2. Setup Nginx and SSL
./scripts/setup-nginx.sh

# 3. Deploy and update services
./scripts/deploy.sh
```

### Railway + Vercel

For the recommended split deployment, use Railway for the Express/PostgreSQL backend and Vercel for the Next.js frontend. Follow [`Docs/RAILWAY_VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT.md`](Docs/RAILWAY_VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT.md) for root directories, environment variables, migrations, health checks, and the one-time herb/knowledge-base bootstrap.

---

## Automated Testing

Use the root-level [`HERBAL_AI_TESTING_SCRATCHPAD.md`](HERBAL_AI_TESTING_SCRATCHPAD.md) for manual session notes, quick regression commands, evidence capture, and temporary-data cleanup. Confirmed outcomes belong in `Docs/TEST_EXECUTION_LOG.md`.

Run the automated Vitest test suites (83 tests across authentication/account recovery, profile authorization and validation, safe post-login session caching, bounded user lookup batching, production error responses, herbs, suggestions, chat, system features, validation, fallback behavior, forum deletion and cache controls; some integration checks require the configured database and Gemini API):

```bash
cd herbalaibackend
npm test
```

Run TypeScript compilation checks:
```bash
# Backend
cd herbalaibackend && npx tsc --noEmit

# Frontend
cd herbalaifrontend && npx tsc --noEmit
```

### Performance controls

- Public herb queries use a bounded in-memory cache with automatic invalidation after library changes.
- The frontend deduplicates concurrent herb/session/notification GET requests.
- Messenger history uses a 50-message cursor and can load older pages on demand.
- API responses expose `Server-Timing` and `X-Response-Time`; slow requests are logged as structured JSON.
- Dr. Ai reports separate embedding, retrieval, and generation timings without logging question content.

Optional tuning values are documented in `.env.example`: `HERB_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `AUTH_USER_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `AUTH_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, `SLOW_REQUEST_THRESHOLD_MS`, `DR_AI_MAX_COSINE_DISTANCE`, and the bounded `DB_POOL_*` connection-pool settings. Slow-request logs include a pool snapshot (`total`, `idle`, and `waiting`) to identify database saturation. The authentication-user cache is intentionally short-lived and is invalidated immediately by application-managed ban, verification, and password changes.

Email safety is controlled by `EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE`: use `log` for local development, `allowlist` plus `EMAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS` for controlled mailbox testing, and `live` only for production. Development defaults to `log` when the variable is omitted.
On Railway Free, Trial, or Hobby, SMTP is blocked. Use an HTTPS mail provider: either `EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend` with a verified sender domain, or `EMAIL_PROVIDER=gmail` with a dedicated Gmail API OAuth client and refresh token for an existing Gmail sender. See `Docs/RAILWAY_VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT.md`. Failed verification delivery leaves a recoverable unverified account, so use the resend-verification action rather than signing up again.
`REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false` is a temporary, explicit fallback: it skips verification email during signup and permits password login for unverified accounts without marking their addresses verified. It weakens identity assurance. Password recovery still requires working email delivery. After deploying the `email_verification_required` migration and matching backend, existing accounts created during this fallback retain password login; newly registered password accounts must verify when the setting returns to `true`. Restore it only after mail delivery is reliable.
The forgot-password endpoint keeps its existing per-IP limit and permits at most one accepted reset email per account in a rolling hour. Repeated and unknown-address requests receive the same neutral response; a failed or suppressed delivery releases the per-account cooldown so the user can retry. Reset links expire after one hour.

---

## Administrative Account

Before running `npm run seed`, configure `ADMIN_EMAIL` and a unique random `ADMIN_PASSWORD` of at least 12 characters. The project does not ship a default administrator password. Never commit production credentials.

---

# IFT 401 Team 2 Capstone

A team-developed stock trading simulation created for **IFT 401: Information Technology Capstone** at Arizona State University.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is an educational simulation. It does not execute real trades or provide financial advice.

## Project Status

## Local Setup

See the **[Development Setup Guide](docs/development-setup.md)** for complete environment, database, server, and testing instructions.

The standard setup uses a local Python virtual environment, dependencies pinned in `requirements.txt`, environment variables copied from `.env.example`, and SQLite for local development.

Never commit `.env`, credentials, API keys, database exports, or real user information.

## Planned Technology Stack

| Area | Technology |
|---|---|
| Language | Python |
| Web framework | Django |
| Frontend | Django templates, HTML, CSS, Bootstrap, and limited JavaScript |
| Database access | Django ORM |
| Local database | SQLite |
| Hosted database | MySQL |
| Authentication | Django authentication |
| Testing | Django test framework |
| Deployment | PythonAnywhere |
| Collaboration | GitHub |

The stack is the team's current baseline and may be revised if a documented project requirement or technical constraint makes a change necessary.

## Team

- Nathan Able
- Christy
- Steeve

## Collaboration Workflow

New collaborators should begin with the **[First GitHub Collaboration Exercise](docs/first-github-collaboration-exercise.md)**.

1. Synchronize your local copy of `main`.
2. Create a short-lived branch for one task.
3. Commit focused changes with a clear message.
4. Push the branch and open a pull request into `main`.
5. Have another team member review the pull request.
6. Merge only after review and required checks pass.

Do not commit directly to `main`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for naming conventions and the complete workflow.

## Local Setup

Detailed setup commands will be added when the Django project is initialized. The expected workflow will be:

1. Clone the repository.
2. Create and activate a Python virtual environment.
3. Install dependencies from `requirements.txt`.
4. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`.
5. Apply database migrations.
6. Start the Django development server.

Never commit `.env`, credentials, API keys, database exports, or real user information.

- [First GitHub collaboration exercise](docs/first-github-collaboration-exercise.md)
- [Contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md)

This repository contains student work produced for an ASU course. Assignment instructions, grading materials, instructor-only resources, teammate personal information, and credentials must not be committed to this public repository.

No open-source license has been selected. The code remains viewable publicly, but reuse permission has not been granted. Licensing may be reconsidered only with team approval.

# 🌍 GeoShop: Global Location-Based Product Search & Price-Comparison Platform ![GeoShop Platform](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1451187580459-43490279c0fa?w=1200&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80) **GeoShop** is a production-quality, location-based product discovery and shopping platform comparison platform built for MSc Software Systems / Full-Stack Development. It enables customers to search for any product, visualize worldwide store availability as pins on an interactive **3D rotating Earth globe**, evaluate multi-merchant prices, ratings, verified reviews, and derived Quality Scores across platforms (e.g. Amazon, Flipkart, MediaMarkt, Rakuten), and seamlessly redirect to the original merchant product pages to complete purchases. GeoShop operates strictly as a **discovery & comparison layer**—it never processes payments or impersonates storefronts. --- ## 🌟 Key Features 1. **Interactive 3D World Globe (Three.js & WebGL)** - **Local Photorealistic Textures**: Bundled 2K day, normal/bump, specular, and cloud maps for 100% offline functionality. - **Custom Atmospheric Fresnel Shader**: Dynamic atmosphere glow with smooth color shifts matching the selected country (e.g., *Cyber Saffron* for India 🇮🇳, *Cyber Cyan* for USA 🇺🇸, *Sakura Crimson* for Japan 🇯🇵, *Emerald Aurora* for Germany 🇩🇪). - **Independent Orbiting Cloud Layer**: Realistic volumetric atmospheric drift. - **Accurate Geodesic Mapping**: UV-calibrated spherical coordinates (`latLongToVector3`). - **Damped Inertia & Idle Auto-Rotate**: Smooth OrbitControls rotation that pauses on user interaction and auto-resumes after 4 seconds of inactivity. - **Gesture Discriminator**: 5px threshold cleanly separates dragging from clicking; 250ms debounce differentiates single-click (fly-to) from double-click (comparison matrix). 2. **Price Pulse & Animated Deal Arcs** - **Price Pulse Color Tiers**: Country pins dynamically pulse based on relative price: - 🟢 **Green**: Global Best Price / Cheapest ($\le 10\%$ of minimum) - 🟡 **Amber**: Mid-tier regional price ($10\% - 30\%$ above minimum) - 🔴 **Red**: Higher price / Tariffs ($> 30\%$ above minimum) - **Animated Deal Arcs**: Parabolic 3D Bézier curves arching over the globe from the selected country to cheaper destinations with traveling pulse particles and interactive savings tags (e.g. `⚡ Save 17% ($250) in USA 🇺🇸`). - **Permanent Legend**: Glassmorphic Price Pulse & Deal Arcs legend anchored to the viewport. 3. **Multi-Store Price & Quality Comparison Engine** - **Normalized Multi-Currency Engine**: Compares prices in local currencies (₹ INR, $ USD, £ GBP, € EUR, ¥ JPY, A$ AUD, AED, R$ BRL) alongside standardized USD conversions. - **30-Day SVG Price Sparklines**: Historical regional price trends for each merchant listing. - **"Best Time to Buy" Advice**: Dynamic hints (`Historical low - buy now`, `Good time to buy`, or `Price is stable`). - **Algorithmic Winner Badges**: Flags **Best Price**, **Best Quality**, and **Best Value**. - **Side-by-Side Cross-Country Mode**: Compare listings across up to 3 countries simultaneously. 4. **Transparent 5-Factor Quality Index (0-100)** - Algorithmic scoring that prevents seller manipulation: - **40% Customer Rating Component**: Star ratings normalized to 40 points. - **30% Review Volume Component**: Log-scaled review count to reflect statistical confidence. - **30% Seller Trust Component**: Historical seller reliability and fulfillment record. - **Consumer Rights Shield**: 30-day hassle-free return policy verification. - **Anti-Price-Gouging Check**: Flags listings with inflated pricing (>20% above 30-day historical median). 5. **Direct Merchant Redirection** - Clicking **BUY / VISIT STORE** triggers celebratory confetti visual feedback and opens the original merchant search URL in a new tab with strict `rel="noopener noreferrer"` protection and demonstration disclaimers. 6. **Search, History & Mission-Control Navigation** - **300ms Debounced Search**: Fast search bar with keyboard-navigable autocomplete suggestions (↑/↓/Enter). - **Popular Pills**: `iPhone`, `Laptop`, `Headphones`, `Shoes`, `Smart Watch`, `Camera`, `PS5`. - **Search-to-Globe Auto-Fly**: Selecting any product maps pins and automatically eases the 3D camera to the cheapest country pin. - **Database-Backed History**: Audit trail stored in SQLite/PostgreSQL with re-run, single delete, and clear-all actions. - **Command Palette (Ctrl+K)**: Quick search, country jump, and navigation palette. - **Saved Drawer**: Bookmarked listings persisted to database with Framer Motion spring transitions. --- ## 🏗️ Architecture & Technology Stack ```mermaid graph TD Client["React 19 Client (Vite + TypeScript)"] subgraph Frontend["Frontend Layer"] Globe["Three.js 3D WebGL Engine
(Lazy Loaded Chunk)"] Hero["Debounced Search & Command Palette"] Modal["Comparison Matrix & Quality Breakdown"] Drawer["Framer Motion Saved Drawer"] end subgraph Backend["Express.js Server Layer"] Security["Helmet + CORS + Rate Limiter"] Validator["Zod Input Schemas"] Controller["Products, Locations, Websites, History, Saved Controllers"] PricingEngine["Pricing & Quality Math Engine"] end subgraph Database["Prisma ORM Layer"] DB[("SQLite (Dev) / PostgreSQL (Prod)")] end Client --> Globe Client --> Hero Client --> Modal Client --> Drawer Hero & Modal & Drawer -->|REST API Requests| Security Security --> Validator Validator --> Controller Controller --> PricingEngine Controller --> DB ``` ### Technology Matrix | Layer | Technologies | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Frontend Framework** | React 19, TypeScript, Vite | Fast rendering, strict type-safety, rapid HMR | | **3D Graphics** | Three.js (WebGL), Custom GLSL Shaders, OrbitControls | 60 FPS interactive rotating Earth, pins, Deal Arcs, atmosphere | | **Styling & Motion** | Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, Lucide Icons, Canvas-Confetti | Glassmorphic dark UI, micro-animations, spring drawers | | **Backend Runtime** | Node.js, Express.js, TypeScript | REST API architecture, central error handling | | **Database & ORM** | Prisma ORM (SQLite / PostgreSQL) | Strongly-typed relational data model, automated migrations | | **Security** | Helmet, express-rate-limit, CORS, Zod validation | HTTP headers hardening, rate limiting, strict payload parsing | | **Testing** | Vitest (18 passing unit & API tests) | Fast native TypeScript test runner | --- ## 🗄️ Relational Data Model (Mermaid ER Diagram) ```mermaid erDiagram Location ||--o{ Website : "hosts" Location ||--o{ SearchHistory : "filters" Website ||--o{ Listing : "offers" Product ||--o{ Listing : "cataloged_as" Product ||--o{ SearchHistory : "queried_for" Listing ||--o{ SavedItem : "bookmarked_as" Location { string id PK string name string code float lat float lon string currency string atmosphereColor } Website { string id PK string name string locationId FK string baseSearchUrl float trustScore } Product { string id PK string name string brand string category string imageEmoji string description } Listing { string id PK string productId FK string websiteId FK float price string currency float rating int reviewCount boolean inStock int returnDays string priceHistory } SearchHistory { string id PK string query string productId FK string locationId FK datetime searchedAt } SavedItem { string id PK string listingId FK datetime savedAt } ``` --- ## ⚡ Quick Start & Installation (< 5 Minutes) ### Prerequisites - **Node.js**: `v18.0.0` or higher - **npm**: `v9.0.0` or higher ### 1. Backend Setup & Seeding ```bash cd backend npm install npm run db:generate npm run db:push npm run db:seed npm run dev ``` *Backend runs on `http://localhost:5000` (`/api/health` reports status).* ### 2. Frontend Setup Open a second terminal window: ```bash cd frontend npm install npm run dev ``` *Frontend application runs on `http://localhost:5173`.* --- ## 🧪 Testing Run backend unit and integration tests with Vitest: ```bash cd backend npm test ``` *Executes 18 tests verifying currency conversion, Quality Index math, Price Pulse tiers, and REST API endpoints.* --- ## 📡 REST API Reference | Method | Endpoint | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `GET` | `/api/health` | Service health status and phase identifier | | `GET` | `/api/products` | Retrieve all catalog products | | `GET` | `/api/products/search?q=...` | Debounced product search with AI discovery analysis | | `GET` | `/api/products/:id` | Get detailed product specifications | | `GET` | `/api/products/:id/availability` | Get 3D Globe location pins, lat/lon, and lowest regional prices | | `GET` | `/api/products/:id/compare?locationId=...` | Side-by-side merchant store listings, sparklines, and quality score | | `GET` | `/api/locations` | List 8 global countries with atmosphere colors | | `GET` | `/api/websites` | List supported shopping platforms | | `GET` | `/api/history` | Retrieve search query audit trail | | `POST` | `/api/history` | Record a search query | | `DELETE` | `/api/history/:id` | Delete individual search query | | `DELETE` | `/api/history` | Clear all search history | | `GET` | `/api/saved` | Retrieve bookmarked store listings | | `POST` | `/api/saved` | Save / bookmark a store listing | | `DELETE` | `/api/saved/:id` | Remove a bookmarked listing | --- ## 🚀 Production Deployment Guide ### Production Deployment (Vercel & Railway) 👉 **See the complete step-by-step guide in [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)** 1. **Push to GitHub**: Push the repository to GitHub (`git push -u origin main`). 2. **Deploy Backend on Railway**: - Create a project on [Railway](https://railway.app), deploy from GitHub, set Root Directory to `/backend`. - Add a **PostgreSQL** database service in Railway. - Set environment variables (`DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV=production`, `CORS_ORIGIN=*`, `JWT_SECRET`). - Run `npm run db:setup` in Railway to initialize tables and populate seed data. - Generate a public domain (e.g. `https://geoshop-backend.up.railway.app`). 3. **Deploy Frontend on Vercel**: - Import project in [Vercel](https://vercel.com), set Root Directory to `frontend`. - Set `VITE_API_BASE_URL` to your Railway domain ending with `/api` (e.g., `https://geoshop-backend.up.railway.app/api`). - Click **Deploy**. --- ## 📚 Documentation & Viva Defense Resources - **[5-Minute Live Viva Demo Script](docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md)**: Structured walkthrough for live examiner evaluations. - **[20 Viva Examination Questions & Answers](docs/VIVA_QA.md)**: Detailed technical explanations covering Three.js, shaders, algorithms, and Prisma. - **[5-Phase Verification Checklist](docs/CHECKLIST.md)**: Complete feature verification matrix. --- ## 📜 Limitations & Future Work - **Live Affiliate API Webhooks**: Current development uses a seed layer. Production can integrate Amazon Creator API and Flipkart Affiliate API. - **Real-Time Exchange Rates**: Can connect to open exchange rate APIs (e.g. Open Exchange Rates) for live hourly forex updates. - **GeoIP Localization**: Auto-detecting customer country via MaxMind GeoIP on first load. --- ## ⚖️ License & Disclaimers - GeoShop is designed as an educational full-stack capstone project for MSc Software Systems / Full Stack Development. - All merchant logos and trademarks (Amazon, Flipkart, MediaMarkt, Rakuten, etc.) belong to their respective owners.
